About Tutor 

 We believe robots should be the next chapter in making physical labor safer and more affordable. But most American factories and warehouses still don’t have a single robot. Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

 

 We build robots that go straight into real factories and warehouses, to do real work, with real impact. Our robots move boxes, pallets and bulk goods, and pick and pack with human-like dexterity, for family-owned manufacturers and some of the largest brands in the world. Every robot learns on the job, and each one we deploy makes the next one more capable, more affordable and faster to put to work.

 

 Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, we do it all in-house: the robotics hardware, the machine learning, and the field deployment and service.

 

 The Role 

 You are our first Head of Supply Chain, reporting to the CTO. Your mandate: the supply base never limits how fast we build and deploy robots.

 

 You’ll build the function from the ground up (the team, the supplier base, the planning engine and the tools) and run it on data and engineering judgment, not spreadsheets. You’ll build strong relationships and partnerships with our suppliers so they grow as we grow, sit at the table from first CAD, and drive cost down initatives.

 How we hire 

 We care more about what you’ve built than years or titles. In interviews you’ll walk us through a supply base you built, a supplier you turned around and a negotiation you won.

 

 Compensation 

 $220,000 to $280,000 base, depending on experience, plus equity. On-site in Watertown, MA.

 

 Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds. 

 What you’ll own
 Sourcing and the Asia supply base 


 Set commodity strategy across mechanical, electrical and electronic components

 Eliminate single sources on critical components. Qualify second sources in Asia and onshore where it makes sense

 Develop suppliers into partners that add capacity and grow with us

 Select and manage contract manufacturers

 Negotiate contracts, pricing and capacity, and drive BOM cost down every quarter


 Procurement and planning 


 Own purchasing end to end

 Turn the build plan into a supply plan: MRP, long-lead buys, safety stock and clear-to-build

 Own supply chain’s role in the ECO process: cost, lead-time and inventory impact, cut-ins and supplier notifications

 Own the supply chain systems and decide what we build, buy or automate next


 Logistics and trade 


 Inbound freight from Asia and outbound shipping to customers in the US and Canada

 Customs, tariffs, landed cost and hazmat compliance

 3PL partners


 How you’ll work 


 Inside NPI, at the table from first CAD, not handed a frozen BOM

 No silos with Engineering, Manufacturing or Quality

 Build your own tools to track supplier risk, lead time and cost in real time


 The two systems you’ll build
 You’ll build these with your team and run the supply chain on them.

 

 1. Line-down prevention: the line never stops for a part 


 One live view from deployment schedule to dock: build plan, BOM, inventory, open POs and supplier capacity

 Early warning on shortages, with an owner and recovery plan

 Supplier health scoring and automatic expedite, buffer and second-source triggers


 2. Cost-down engine: cost goes down every quarter by design 


 Should-cost models and true landed cost, so we negotiate from facts

 A savings pipeline tracked from idea to realized savings

 Cost and sourcing risk fed back into design early


 What success looks like in year one

 90 days: Supply base mapped by commodity, with risk, lead time and capacity for every critical part. Team hired or in flight

 6 months: Second sources shipping for our highest-risk components. Supply base ready for our second product line

 12 months: No supplier limits a build at target rate. BOM cost on a committed downward path. Supply plan, scorecards and cost tracked live


 Your team
 You’ll inherit a small, hands-on group and build the rest: supplier development and engineering in the US and China, contract manufacturing, electronics sourcing, purchasing, planning and logistics.

 

 We run a lean core and scale with contractors. You decide the shape.

 Who you are

 You’ve taken a hardware supply chain from startup to volume production, ideally in robotics or complex electromechanical systems

 You know electromechanical commodities, from fabricated and cast parts to electronics, motion and power

 You’ve developed suppliers in Asia in person and can tell one that can scale from one that can’t

 You’ve managed contract manufacturers and taken real cost out through negotiation and design changes

 You’ve led NPI sourcing from early design through ramp

 You build and lead teams, and still get your hands dirty

 You negotiate hard and keep the relationship

 You’re technical enough to challenge engineers on design-for-supply

 You’re able to travel internationally, about 25% of the time


 Strong signals

 You’ve stood up ERP/MRP or supply chain tooling from nothing, and know when not to

 You’ve moved work to contract manufacturers and made it stick

 You’ve worked across US, Canada and Asia operations


 This role is not for you if

 You need established processes and a large team to be effective

 You think supply chain starts when Engineering releases the BOM


 Benefits

 Fully employer-covered health insurance , so you’re protected without the premium.

 A managed 401(k) to help you plan for the future.

 Generous time off: unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off.

 Regular in-office meals and team social events throughout the year.

 We’re seeking a Director, Metals who’s ready to be part of a people-first company offering best-in-class products, exceptional training, and deep industry pride—all built to help our partners and team succeed. 
 ABOUT THE ROLE 
 The Director, Metals will serve as the senior business leader for the Elevate Metals business, with responsibility for driving overall business performance, growth, profitability, operational and procurement excellence, and strategic direction. This leader will oversee the Metals organization as a key business within Elevate while also partnering closely with other sales and commercial leaders throughout Building Envelope. 
 
 WHAT YOU'LL ACCOMPLISH 
 Provide overall leadership and strategic direction for the Elevate Metals business, with accountability for business performance, growth, profitability, and operational results. 
 Develop and execute the Metals business strategy in alignment with Elevate single ply systems and Building Envelope objectives. 
 Analyze metals market trends and report key insights to leadership, identifying potential M&A opportunities. 
 Own key business performance metrics, including revenue, profitability, margin, productivity, working capital, service levels, and operational efficiency. 
 Lead regular business reviews and communicate performance, trends, opportunities, and risks to executive leadership.

 Advanced degree

About Tutor

 We believe robots are the biggest lever we have to making the physical world a better, more affordable place. But robots are a rounding error in our society: nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t even have a single robot, and robots have yet to make their way into our homes or places of business.

 Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

 Tutor is a robotics research and deployment company, building generally capable robot hardware and artificial intelligence to enable robots to go where no robots have gone before. Our robots range from a semi-humanoid with frontier dexterity approaching the human form to workhorses that do back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for businesses from family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Tutor robots are manufactured at scale and operate as a network, combining the whole fleet’s learned experience to train ever more capable robot artificial intelligence.

 Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, our team is full stack: we design and manufacture robot hardware, train our own models, work directly with the smallest and largest end-customers, and maintain our fleet across the United States. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

 Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

 Why Tutor?

 Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

 Our team is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

 Benefits

 We take care of our team so they can do their best work. At Tutor, you’ll get:

 
 Fully employer-covered health insurance, so you’re protected without the premium.

 A managed 401(k) to help you plan for the future.

 Generous time off: unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.

 Regular in-office meals and team social events throughout the year.

 
 As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.

 Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.

 The Role
 You lead our Production Engineering team: the engineers and technicians who take robot designs from prototype to mass production. You report to the Head of Manufacturing.

 Your job is to design the system and the machine that build our robots: the processes, test systems, tooling and change control that let Manufacturing produce high-quality robots at a competitive cost, even as designs change fast.

 This is a player-coach role. You set direction, assign the work and grow the team, and you stay hands-on. You are in design reviews, at the bench with a scope, and on the floor debugging a robot that needs to ship.

 Why This Role Matters
 Every robot we ship has to be built right, tested right and delivered on time, while the design behind it keeps improving. That only works with a strong team and a production system built for change. Much of that system doesn't exist yet. You build it, and the team that runs it.

 What You'll Own

 Lead the team: Set priorities and assign work across production engineers, test and bring-up engineers, technicians and contract engineers. Hold clear technical standards and review the team's work.

 Grow the team: Hire, mentor and develop engineers. Shape a team structure that scales as production grows.

 Prototype to production: Own how new designs move from prototype through pilot builds into volume production, with the processes, work instructions, tooling, fixtures and station design to support them.

 Test and bring-up: Own the test strategy across the line, from subassembly bench tests to station tests, robot bring-up and final acceptance, so defects are caught early and never reach a customer.

 Engineering change: Represent Manufacturing in design change reviews and own how changes are cut in on the line without losing quality or output.

 Design for manufacturing: Partner with hardware engineering so designs arrive buildable, testable, serviceable and cost-effective.

 Recurring failures: Use data from the line and the field to drive recurring problems to root cause and permanent fixes.

 Stay hands-on: Debug electrical, mechanical and system-level issues yourself when a robot needs to ship.


 What Success Looks Like
 In your first few months: You've worked the floor with the team and earned their trust. Every engineer knows their priorities and what they own. The top recurring build failures have clear root causes and fixes underway, and you've laid out a plan for test, change control and the team.

 In your first year: Robots move through bring-up and final test with little rework. Design changes reach the line cleanly. New designs arrive production-ready. The team is growing, owns its work and holds a high bar without you in the room.

 Required

 Bachelor's in Electrical, Mechanical, Computer or Mechatronics Engineering. A Master's is a plus.

 Proven experience leading engineers: setting priorities, assigning work, reviewing output and developing people. A formal manager or technical lead title both count. We care about what you did with the team you had.

 Deep hands-on hardware experience designing, integrating and debugging complex electromechanical systems. You still find root cause yourself.

 Strong electrical fundamentals. You read schematics, use scopes and meters, and isolate problems across power, boards, harnesses, sensors, actuators and communication interfaces.

 Experience taking hardware from prototype through new product introduction into volume production.

 Experience building production test systems: fixtures, bring-up, end-of-line or automated test.

 Hands-on design-for-manufacturing and design-for-test work with design engineering.

 Experience managing engineering change on an active production line.

 You use AI tools daily in your engineering work and can show us how.


 Preferred

 Built or scaled a production or manufacturing engineering team at a hardware startup.

 Robotics or industrial automation experience.

 Cost reduction work: should-cost, value engineering, or BOM and labor reduction.

 Python for test automation, diagnostics or data analysis.

 Experience with MES, traceability or change control systems.

 Contract manufacturer or supplier bring-up.


 Why Join

 Build the team and the system. You shape how we build robots and who builds them.

 Lead without leaving the hardware. You manage a team and still get your hands dirty.

 Real hardware, real stakes. Your fixes run on robots working at customer sites.

 AI is how we work. You have the tools and the backing to automate what most factories still do by hand.

 Direct line to leadership. Work side by side with hardware, software and deployment teams.


 How We Work: Our Values in This Role
 We hire against our values, and we'll interview you against them too. Here's what they look like in this seat:


 Love of the Game. You lead from the bench, not from a slide deck.

 Gumption. When a robot won't ship, you and your team are already on the floor finding out why.

 Beginner's Mindset. You question how we build and test today, and you change your mind fast when the data says to.

 Belief in Each Other. You give your engineers real ownership, help them grow, and earn the hardware team's respect by being right and being fair.

 Keep Moving Forward. You find the fix that keeps the line moving today, then make it permanent.

 Customer Obsession. Every shortcut on the line shows up at a customer site. You and your team build it right.

At AstraZeneca, we are building the supply capabilities needed to deliver the next generation of cell therapies to patients around the world. As Senior Director, Delivery, you will lead the global enabling team responsible for strengthening and protecting the third-party supplier ecosystem across our Cell Therapy portfolio.
 You will shape how we anticipate supplier risk, build strategic supplier relationships and secure the direct materials and external capabilities needed to support in-vivo, autologous and allogeneic cell therapies. Your leadership will help move the organization from reactive escalation toward proactive supply assurance, creating resilient, scalable supply networks that can grow from clinical development through commercial delivery.
 Based in Gaithersburg Maryland, this role reports to the Executive Director, External Supply & Delivery and includes global travel to suppliers as needed.
 Why This Role 
 Cell therapy supply chains operate with extraordinary complexity. Materials, manufacturing partners, logistics providers and technology platforms must perform reliably against highly regulated requirements and patient-critical timelines.
 In this role, you will have the opportunity to:
 Build the Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) and supplier risk frameworks that shape how Cell Therapy manages its global external ecosystem.
 Provide forward-looking visibility of supplier and supply continuity risks across the Cell Therapy portfolio.
 Strengthen strategic partnerships with critical suppliers and prepare the supplier network for global commercial scale.
 Improve on-time, in-full (OTIF) performance and reduce the risk of patient-impacting supply disruptions.
 Advance dual-sourcing, business continuity, supplier development and new material introduction strategies.
 Use analytics, digital capabilities and AI to strengthen risk monitoring, supplier performance and supply assurance.
 Develop a global team with expertise spanning supplier risk, SRM, direct materials and supply assurance.
 Accountabilities 
 Supplier Risk & Portfolio Resilience 
 Develop, own and continuously improve the Risk Framework for External Supply & Delivery, including supplier risk assessment, risk taxonomy and scoring, mitigation standards, escalation triggers, business continuity and contingency planning.
 Lead risk management at the Cell Therapy Technical Operations (CTTO) portfolio level, maintaining consolidated, forward-looking visibility across CDMOs, direct materials, equipment and services, and logistics suppliers.
 Lead strategies addressing single-source dependencies, dual sourcing, alternate supplier identification, new material introduction (NMI) and product lifecycle risk.
 Strengthen resilience for critical plasmids, raw materials, cold chain and other supply dependencies.
 Maintain visibility of supplier sub-tier (n-1), geopolitical and China-related supply risks, including relevant BIOSECURE considerations.
 Drive mitigation actions to closure in partnership with External Supply, Quality, Planning and other stakeholders.
 Supplier Relationship Management 
 Develop and lead the enterprise Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) framework, including supplier segmentation, governance, service-level agreement (SLA) performance, scorecards, quarterly business reviews and continuous improvement.
 Establish and govern the Preferred Supplier List (PSL), helping identify suppliers positioned to support future clinical and commercial requirements.
 Establish expectations for root-cause analysis and corrective and preventive action (CAPA) within supplier performance management.
 Build consistent supplier performance dashboards covering portfolio health, on-time delivery, quality events, value delivery and suppliers at risk.
 Enable consistent adoption of the Risk and SRM frameworks across External Supply, Direct and Indirect Sourcing, Automation & Robotics and China operations.
 Critical Supplier & Logistics Partnerships 
 Lead strategic relationships with portfolio-critical suppliers across key materials, logistics, technology and platform capabilities.

Position Overview
 The Product Engineer – Chassis Mounts is responsible for the system-level design, development, validation, timing, and engineering release of powertrain mounts, differential mounts, cradle mounts, Electric Drive Module (EDM) mounts, body mounts, and adapter brackets. The engineer executes a comprehensive work plan to meet component and system-level functional objectives, delivering quality components on time from initial concept through vehicle launch.
 Key Responsibilities
 Design & System Integration
 CAD & Packaging: Lead system design, CAD packaging (NX), and release of chassis powertrain mounts, EDM mounts, body mounts, and related bracketry.

 PLM & BOM Management: Ensure model and drawing integrity in PLM/Teamcenter system, manage the Engineering Bill of Materials (EBOM), and write Engineering Change Notices (CN).

 Joint Design: Design fastened joints and lead assembly torque development and validation.

 Cross-Functional & Attribute Balancing
 Attribute Integration: Work closely with support groups—including NVH (Noise, Vibration, and Harshness), Vehicle Dynamics, Vehicle Integration, Stress Lab, and CAE—to execute validation and testing.

 Functional Trade-Offs: Balance mount stiffness, isolation, fatigue life, and durability attributes to meet vehicle-level functional objectives.

 Validation & Engineering Quality
 Quality Documentation: Create, update, and manage component Design Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (DFMEA), Design Verification Plan & Report (DVP&R), and Product Assurance Plans (PAP).

 Testing Execution: Support physical system testing in labs and vehicle-level dynamic/NVH testing.

 Problem Solving: Lead root-cause problem solving for mount-related issues using structured issue-tracking systems.

 Supplier & Assembly Plant Support
 Supplier Management: Manage Tier-1 mount suppliers to ensure technical requirements, cost, weight, and timing targets are met.

 Launch Support: Provide hands-on build support at OEM assembly plants and supplier manufacturing facilities during prototype and production launch phases.

 The Chassis Quality Engineer is responsible for driving component, system, and assembly-level quality for chassis commodities across product development, launch, and mass production phases. All Memphis plant employees report directly or indirectly to this position; overall accountability for ~ 8 reports. 
 
 The Plant Manager directly supports Plant Staff to manage activities and lead continued improvement in the areas of Operations, Maintenance, Human Resources, Engineering, Accounting, Purchasing, Quality, and Laboratories.  The PM possesses a strong, working knowledge and ensures compliance related to all external regulatory requirements, industry best practices, and internal policies and procedures (specifically capital, accounting, purchasing, and HES).  This position requires a strong change management leader to manage the business growth and integration of new programs.

 Insures plant is in full compliance with Arkema guidance and directives along with all applicable regulations. 
 Foster a culture of “0 is possible” and drives Safety as a core plant value. 
 Directly participates to some core Arkema programs such as BBS. 
 Operations – 50% 
 Ensures that safe operating procedures and practices are in place and followed.  Ensures that mechanical integrity of all plants is maintained or improved to allow safe and efficient operation.  Ensures that plants produce at volumes to meet demand requirements set forth in S&OP plans.  Ensures that adequate training is provided for a safe and efficient plant operations. 
 Human Resources – 10% 
 Ensures that employee activities related to hiring, promotion, layoff, salary, etc. are handled professionally.  Provides an atmosphere for open communication between all employees. 
 Financial –10% 
 Directly accountable to prepare various budgets (fixed, variable and capex) then monitors and controls to insure these budgets are met.

 Mentoring/Coaching:  Develop close working relationships with plant personnel and places a strong focus on improving both individual and team performance supporting programs such as SMART

 Minimum of 15 years of progressive manufacturing experience in plant operations, process design, and engineering, preferably in both a large and small-size integrated process manufacturing company 
 
 Education and area of focus 
 Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering required. 
 
 
 
 Certifications/Trainings: 
 Lean or Six Sigma certification preferred 
 
 Competencies -Knowledge Skills & Abilities (KSAs) 
 Leadership experience in a specialty chemicals or petroleum plant is required. 
 Experience leading continuous improvement initiatives is required. 
 Good knowledge of PC applications (including Microsoft Office suite and SAP) accounting systems and the ability to learn new system processes, preferably SAP experience. 
 Knowledge of latest safety laws and regulations 
 HES Requirement – All Jobs 
 Supports the site HES policy and complies with all regulatory and internal requirements

 Supports and promotes the reporting of all health, safety, environmental, near-miss, accident or injury incidents

At BWX Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: BWXT), we are People Strong, Innovation Driven. A U.S.-based company, BWXT is a Fortune 1000 and Defense News Top 100 manufacturing and engineering innovator that provides safe and effective nuclear solutions for global security, clean energy, environmental restoration, nuclear medicine and space exploration. With more than 7,800 employees, BWXT has 14 major operating sites in the U.S., Canada and the U.K. We are the sole manufacturer of naval nuclear reactors for U.S. submarines and aircraft carriers. Our company supplies precision manufactured components, services and fuel for the commercial nuclear power industry across four continents. Our joint ventures provide environmental restoration and operations management at a dozen U.S. Department of Energy and NASA facilities. BWXT’s technology is driving advances in medical radioisotope production in North America and microreactors for various defense and space applications. For more information, visit www.bwxt.com . Follow us on LinkedIn , X , Facebook and Instagram . 
 
 Welcome to BWXT We believe in empowering our employees and cultivating a dynamic workplace that fosters growth and collaboration. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting your career, you'll find opportunities to challenge yourself, learn from seasoned experts, and contribute to nuclear innovation. We require a diverse range of skills to support our work in the markets that drive our business and welcome candidates from all backgrounds and life stages who are passionate about making a difference. 
 Position Overview: Director of Engineering – Enrichment Operations 
 As the Director of Engineering for BWXT Enrichment Operations, you will lead the full engineering function responsible for delivering a production‑ready centrifuge product and a high‑precision, highly automated factory capability. You will oversee engineering strategy from early concept through prototype/pilot phases to full‑rate production, establishing core systems engineering and systems integration practices to ensure disciplined requirements management, interface control, verification/validation, and seamless subsystem integration. This role is pivotal in standing up a modern digital factory, enabling high‑volume production with aerospace‑grade quality and nuclear regulatory rigor. 
 Location 
 On-site in Oak Ridge, Tennessee 
 Your Day-to-Day as the Director of Engineering 
 Engineering Leadership & Organization • Build, scale, and lead a multidisciplinary engineering organization spanning manufacturing, process, facilities, automation, industrialization, and precision systems. • Serve as the technical authority for manufacturability, scalability, risk management, and readiness. 
 Systems Engineering (SE) • Establish a modern systems engineering capability that includes requirements management, architecture development, interface control (ICDs), configuration management, verification and validation, and model-based systems engineering/digital thread practices. • Define “Definition of Done” at each development gate and ensure complete, build-ready Product Readiness Packs (e.g., BOMs, routers, test plans). 
 Systems Integration (SI) • Lead end‑to‑end integration of subsystems into the centrifuge product and supporting systems. • Develop integration plans, lab capabilities, fixtures, and test regimes to validate subsystem and system-level performance. • Collaborate with the CTO and ORNL Design Authority to align qualification evidence and change packages; support seamless integration with CMDF pilot builds and transfer to CMF industrialization. 
 Factory Design, Construction & Startup • Lead design, build, and commissioning of a high‑precision manufacturing facility. • Integrate automation, robotics, and digital factory systems to enable high throughput, traceability, and tightly controlled processes. 
 Manufacturing Excellence & DFx • Deliver engineering solutions capable of automotive‑pace production with aerospace‑grade quality. • Drive design for manufacturability, assembly, quality, cost, and industrialization (DFM/DFA/DFQ/DFC). 
 Quality, Safety & Compliance • Ensure all engineering designs and processes meet nuclear regulatory, DOE, safety, and BWXT quality requirements. • Embed compliance gates, audit readiness, and pre‑release checks throughout development. 
 Program Controls & Schedule • Partner with Business Operations and Program Controls to maintain a resource‑loaded critical path schedule. • Support earned value management (EVM) discipline and weekly KPI reviews (SPI/CPI, cost variance, schedule adherence). 
 Supply Chain & Technical Readiness • Define technical acceptance criteria for supplier parts, processes, tooling, and special manufacturing steps. • Support supplier onboarding speed, delivery performance, and technical readiness to protect schedule-critical components. 
 Cross-Functional Collaboration • Work closely with CMDF (prototype/pilot operations), CMF (full-rate industrialization), the CTO/Technology organization, and Operations. • Drive the transition from low‑rate initial production (LRIP) to full‑rate production (FRP) on cost and schedule. 
 Required Qualifications 
 • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (advanced degree preferred). • Fifteen (15+) years of progressive engineering leadership in high‑precision, highly regulated manufacturing environments (nuclear, aerospace, defense, automotive, semiconductor, or similar). • Demonstrated experience designing, building, commissioning, and scaling a high‑precision manufacturing facility to high‑volume production. • Strong expertise in advanced manufacturing, automation, precision machining, assembly, metrology, and inspection systems. • Must be a U.S. citizen capable of obtaining and maintaining a DOE Q clearance; active clearance preferred. • Proven ability to lead large, multidisciplinary engineering teams in a fast-paced, highly technical environment. 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 • Experience with automotive‑scale manufacturing and assembly; Lean/Six Sigma leadership. • Hands-on experience deploying Industry 4.0, digital thread, digital twin, and smart factory systems. • Experience guiding organizations from prototype/pilot phases to high‑rate production in startup‑like or greenfield environments. 
 What We Offer 
 • Competitive compensation and benefits package, including health, dental, and retirement plans. • Flexible work schedules and paid time off to promote a healthy work-life balance (as applicable). • Professional development opportunities, including mentorship programs, leadership training, and support for continuing education. • An inclusive atmosphere that celebrates diverse perspectives and enables collaboration across all generations. • The opportunity to shape a mission‑driven organization advancing the future of energy and national security. • Continuous learning and development opportunities to support long‑term career growth. Pay: $200,000 - $271,000 
 
 The base salary range for this position in Tennessee (US-TN) at the start of employment is expected to be between $200,000 and $271,000 per year. However, the base salary offered is based on local job market factors, and may vary further depending on factors specific to the selected job candidate, such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and other objective business considerations. Subject to these considerations, the total compensation package for this position may also include other elements, such as an annual cash incentive in addition to a full range of medical, retirement, and/or other benefits. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided at such time the selected job candidate receives an offer of employment. If hired, the selected job candidate will be employed 'at-will,’ unless employed at a location and in a position subject to a collective bargaining agreement.  The company further reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payment, compensation or benefit program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, company or individual department/team performance, and other market factors. 
 
 As a federal government contractor, BWX Technologies, Inc. and any subsidiaries, affiliates and related entities (“BWXT” or the “Company”) complies with all federal, state, and local laws and customer requirements regarding health and safety protocols.  As such, all BWXT new hires will be required to adhere to applicable Company health and safety requirements within the workplace as a condition of employment. 
 
 All candidates must be U.S. citizens. Selected applicants are required to successfully complete a pre-employment check and drug screening. In addition, the position may require the ability to obtain and maintain applicable federal eligibility requirements for access to classified/sensitive information or matter which involves an extensive criminal and financial background investigation, drug test, previous employment, and reference verifications. 
 
 BWXT is committed to the concept of Equal Employment Opportunity. We have established procedures to ensure that all personnel actions such as recruitment, compensation, career development, benefits, company-sponsored training and social recreational programs are administered without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, citizenship, age, disability, protected veteran or other protected status. 
 
 BWX Technologies, Inc. and its affiliates and subsidiaries (BWXT) is not responsible for and does not accept any liability for fees or other costs associated with resumes or candidates presented by recruiters or employment agencies, unless a binding, written recruitment agreement between BWXT and the recruiter or agency exists prior to the presentation of candidates or resumes to BWXT and includes the specific services, job openings, and fees to be paid (“Agreement”). BWXT may consider any candidate for whom a recruiter or agency has submitted an unsolicited resume and explicitly reserves the right to hire such candidate(s) without any financial obligation to the recruiter or agency unless an Agreement is in place prior to presentation and such Agreement explicitly encompasses the job opening for which such fees or costs are sought. An email, verbal or other informal contact with any person within BWXT will not create a binding agreement. Agencies or recruiters without an Agreement are directed not to contact any hiring managers of BWXT with recruiting inquiries or resumes. Recruiters and agencies interested in partnering with BWXT may contact BWXT’s Talent Acquisition team at talent_acquisition@bwxt.com. #LI-BT1

Our employees can take advantage of various avenues to advance their careers and realize their dreams. Our top-tier benefits and great retirement packages can help you build a rewarding career and lasting future with the State of Illinois. Position Overview The Division of Behavioral Health and Recovery is seeking to hire an energetic, self-motivated professional to fill the Deputy Director of Quality Management position. This position will organize, plan, execute, control and evaluate the ongoing monitoring of the quality of life and quality of care outcomes of individuals receiving services at State-Operated Psychiatric Hospitals (SOPHs), Develops the structure and productivity indicators for staff who will provide quality monitoring. Essential Functions Serves as Deputy Director of Quality Management. 
 Serves as policy-making official. 
 Serves as the IDHS point of contact to assist in addressing concerns between DBHR hospitals and OIG (Office of Inspector General), Equip for Equality, Guardianship and Advocacy, Human Rights Authority, Accreditation and Certification agencies, community partners, Office of the Auditor General.

 Performs other duties as required or assigned which are reasonably within the scope of the duties enumerated above. Minimum Qualifications Requires a master’s degree in social work from an accredited school of Social Work.

Company Description With over $2B in revenue, 80+ manufacturing facilities across 6 continents and over 9,000 employees worldwide, Signode is a leading manufacturer of a broad spectrum of transit packaging consumables, tools, software, and equipment that optimize end-of-line packaging operations and protect products in transit. Signode brings this extensive product portfolio together under hundreds of trusted brands to offer complete transit packaging solutions to its customers. 
 
We produce strap, stretch and protective packaging. We also manufacture packaging tools and equipment used to apply the bulk packaging materials. These commercial packaging products are used to pack, bundle, unitize, protect, and secure goods during warehousing and transit. Our company is a pioneer in the industrial packaging sector with a long history of customer-focused innovations in materials, processes and automation technology that have revolutionized the sector. 
 
Headquartered in Tampa, Florida, we are proud to be the Transit Packaging Division of Crown Holdings, Inc. We are excited to go to market as Signode and to share the portfolio of products, services and capabilities that make us the world’s premier end-of-line packaging company. Job Description Benefits: Signode offers a comprehensive benefits package to full-time employees, which includes health, dental, vision, 401k, paid time off, life insurance, wellness perks, and more. Benefits begin the month following the hire date. Summary This role is for a Plant Manager who is a true leader, one who can build a strong, positive culture throughout the plant. The position calls for a sharp operational and analytical mind that constantly seeks out, teaches, and leads improvements in Safety Performance, Cost Control, Standardized Processes (LEAN), Production Reporting, and Inventory Control. This is a high-visibility opportunity to lead one of Signode’s most important locations, having a big impact on our ability to deliver a profitable year. Here is what makes this role stand out: Pilot the company’s Operational Excellence system, delivering a glidepath in Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Output, and Morale. Take charge of a major turnaround facility. The right leader is confident yet humble, ready to run a 24/7 site from the bottom up, and understands the sweat and equity required to turn it around. Succeed here, and fast-track your path to the next level. Essential Functions Directly manage and coordinate the activities of various plant departments and sites within Signode. Provide strong leadership to the manufacturing team, fostering a collaborative and results-oriented work environment. Develop and implement strategic plans to achieve production goals, optimize processes, and enhance overall plant efficiency. Communicate, uphold and enforce safety protocols and regulatory compliance to maintain a safe and secure working environment. Responsible for talent management and employee lifecycle activities, from hiring to terminating. Collaborate with senior management to align plant operations with organizational objectives. Monitor and analyze production metrics, ensuring that production targets are met while maintaining high-quality standards. Implement efficiency improvement initiatives and address any bottlenecks or issues in the production process. Efficiently allocate resources, including manpower and equipment, to meet production schedules and deadlines. Collaborate with the maintenance team to ensure optimal functionality of machinery and equipment. Collaborate with the quality control department to ensure that products meet or exceed quality standards. Implement measures to address any deviations or non-conformities in the production process. Develop and manage budgets for the manufacturing facility(s), controlling costs and optimizing resource utilization. Identify cost-saving opportunities and implement measures to improve overall plant profitability. Effectively communicate with senior management, department heads, and front-line staff to ensure clear understanding of goals and objectives. Prepare regular reports on plant performance, production metrics, and other relevant KPIs. Lead and support initiatives for continuous improvement, identifying opportunities to enhance plant processes, reduce waste, and increase overall efficiency. Qualifications Education: Bachelor’s degree in Management, Business, or Engineering. Masters Degree in similar field preferred. Experience: Minimum of 15+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing, with at least 5 -7 years in a managerial or supervisory role.  Previous experience as a plant manager is a must. Financial Acumen with the ability to analyze and forecast data and translate results to better solutions.  With the understanding of general ledger accounting and activity rate costing. Strong knowledge of safety metrics and programs. TPM mastery Previous experience leading a turnaround factory Extrusion technical skills ERP system knowledge a plus. LEAN Manufacturing Training or CI Management Experience (Tier I, II, III) Functional Success Drivers: These competencies are what we require for an individual to be successful in this role. Strategic Skills Leadership Result Oriented Safety & Security Communication (Oral & Written) Analytical Skills Inspiring “Followership” Vision Additional Information All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. The Company does not sponsor for employment-based visas for this position now or in the future. Reasonable Accommodation Statement To perform this job successfully, the individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.  Reasonable Accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities. Signode is committed to providing equal opportunities to all qualified applicants, including providing reasonable accommodations during our recruiting process. If you need any assistance or accommodation in applying for this position, please contact us at [email protected] . It is intended to provide guidelines for job expectations and the employee's ability to perform the position described. It is not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all functions, responsibilities, skills and abilities. Additional functions and requirements may be assigned by supervisors as deemed appropriate. This document does not represent a contract of employment, and the Company reserves the right to change this job description and/or assign tasks for the employee to perform, as the Company may deem appropriate. Signode participates in E-Verify and will provide the Department of Homeland Security your Form I-9 information to confirm your authorization to work in the United States. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.

Description Director of Operations - Wisconsin & Illinois 
 Department: Operations Reports To: COO Location: Wisconsin and Illinois; regular travel between assigned facilities Direct Reports: Assigned General Managers, and Site Managers 
 Summary 
 The Director of Operations leads the operational and financial performance of the company's Wisconsin and Illinois facilities. This position oversees conventional caged and cage-free layer production, pullet operations where assigned, shell egg grading and packing, egg breaking and liquid egg processing, feed mills, and supporting operational functions. 
 The Director translates company strategy into clear site-level priorities, develops strong leaders, and holds teams accountable for safe operations, animal welfare, food safety, customer service, and profitability. This role requires a visible, hands-on leader who drives consistent execution, improves operating practices, and builds collaboration across locations and corporate functions. 
 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Regional Leadership and Accountability 
 Lead regional operations to achieve production, processing, quality, service, and financial goals. 
 Establish clear expectations, performance measures, and operating plans for each facility. 
 Hold General Managers and operational leaders accountable for results, timely corrective actions, and follow-through. 
 Maintain a regular presence at facilities to evaluate conditions, coach leaders, and address operational barriers. 
 Standardize effective practices across locations while accounting for differences in housing systems, equipment, and customer requirements. 
 Communicate performance, risks, resource needs, and recommendations to executive leadership. 
 Live Production and Animal Welfare 
 Oversee conventional caged and cage-free layer operations. 
 Oversee pullet rearing and replacement flock readiness where assigned. 
 Drive flock performance through effective management of production, mortality, livability, egg quality, feed conversion, body weight, and flock uniformity. 
 Ensure consistent execution of ventilation, lighting, water, feeding, litter, and manure management programs. 
 Partner with veterinary and nutrition teams on flock health, disease prevention, vaccination, pest control, and nutrition programs. 
 Ensure compliance with company animal welfare standards and applicable certification and customer requirements. 
 Enforce biosecurity expectations for employees, visitors, equipment, contractors, and transportation. 
 Shell Egg and Breaking Operations 
 Oversee shell egg receiving, grading, packing, storage, and shipping. 
 Oversee egg breaking and liquid egg processing, including pasteurization where applicable. 
 Improve egg recovery, saleable yield, throughput, labor efficiency, equipment utilization, and product quality. 
 Reduce checks, cracks, losses, rework, downtime, and customer complaints. 
 Coordinate production and processing schedules with sales, planning, and logistics to meet customer commitments and manage inventory. 
 Partner with Quality Assurance to maintain sanitation, traceability, food safety programs, audit readiness, and timely corrective actions. 
 Ensure reported production, gradeout, yield, and inventory results are accurate and supported by operational records. 
 Feed Mill Operations 
 Oversee assigned feed mills to ensure safe, reliable, and cost-effective feed manufacturing and delivery. 
 Align mill capacity, production schedules, and delivery plans with flock requirements. 
 Partner with nutrition and procurement teams on ingredient quality, availability, formulation implementation, and inventory management. 
 Ensure controls for batching accuracy, mixing consistency, ingredient receiving, storage, sanitation, and feed traceability. 
 Monitor feed manufacturing costs, shrink, downtime, maintenance needs, and delivery performance. 
 Address feed quality concerns promptly with appropriate technical and operational support. 
 Financial and Business Performance 
 Own regional operating performance against approved budgets and business plans. 
 Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, labor planning, and capital planning for assigned operations. 
 Review site financial results and operating metrics to identify variances, determine root causes, and implement corrective actions. 
 Improve cost per dozen, processing costs, feed manufacturing costs, asset utilization, and overall profitability. 
 Ensure purchasing discipline, accurate inventory controls, and compliance with spending authority. 
 Develop capital requests supported by operational need, expected benefits, financial justification, and implementation plans. 
 Maintenance and Supporting Operations 
 Oversee maintenance, preventive maintenance, equipment reliability, utilities, and facility condition. 
 Support transportation, egg movements, feed delivery, warehousing, and other assigned logistics activities. 
 Ensure effective manure handling, storage, and removal, along with environmental stewardship and housekeeping. 
 Coordinate contractors, construction, equipment installations, and facility improvement projects. 
 Maintain emergency response and business continuity plans for disease events, fires, utility failures, severe weather, and equipment breakdowns. 
 People, Safety, and Culture 
 Build and develop a capable regional leadership team through coaching, succession planning, and performance management. 
 Partner with Human Resources on staffing, retention, training, employee relations, and leadership development. 
 Set clear expectations for professional communication, teamwork, and respectful treatment of employees. 
 Promote a culture in which employees raise concerns, leaders address issues promptly, and commitments are completed. 
 Partner with EHS and site leadership to improve workplace safety, investigate incidents, and close corrective actions. 
 Ensure employees receive appropriate training and have the resources needed to perform their work safely and effectively. 
 Qualifications 
 Bachelor's degree in poultry science, agriculture, operations management, business, or a related field preferred; equivalent relevant experience considered. 
 Typically 10 or more years of progressive agricultural or food manufacturing experience, including significant leadership responsibility across multiple facilities. 
 Strong knowledge of commercial layer production, including conventional caged and cage-free systems. 
 Experience overseeing shell egg processing, egg breaking, and feed mill operations strongly preferred. 
 Demonstrated ability to manage budgets, interpret financial results, and improve operational performance. 
 Working knowledge of animal welfare, biosecurity, food safety, employee safety, and environmental requirements. 
 Proven ability to develop leaders, manage change, resolve problems, and hold teams accountable. 
 Strong communication, planning, analytical, and decision-making skills. 
 Measures of Success 
 Performance will be evaluated through a balanced set of regional and site-level measures, including: 
 Financial: Budget performance, controllable costs, and verified improvement results. 
 Live production: Egg production, mortality, livability, feed conversion, and egg quality. 
 Processing: Yield, recovery, throughput, labor efficiency, downtime, and order fulfillment. 
 Feed mills: Feed quality, manufacturing cost, inventory accuracy, and delivery reliability. 
 People and safety: Leadership development, retention, training completion, safety performance, and corrective action closure. 
 Compliance and execution: Animal welfare and food safety results, data accuracy, audit readiness, and completion of operating and capital priorities. 
 Working Conditions 
 This position requires frequent travel between Wisconsin and Illinois facilities and availability to support operations outside normal business hours when necessary. Work includes time in poultry houses, processing plants, feed mills, and outdoor environments, with required adherence to site biosecurity, food safety, and personal protective equipment procedures. Job Location: Bothell, Washington, USA
Job Requisition ID: 15573
Join our global diversified pharmaceutical company enriching lives through our relentless drive to deliver better health outcomes to our patients. We are all in it together to make a difference. Be a part of a culture that doesn't just wait for change but actively creates it—where your skills and values drive our collective progress and impact.
Reporing to the Director of Quality Operations, the is responsible for the management of Quality Engineering team at Solta Medical and is responsible for developing goals, objectives, procedures, policies, and systems that align with FDA/ISO regulations as well as aligns with the company mission and vision.
Note: The following are meant to be representative but not necessarily all inclusive of the duties and responsibilities for this position title.
Responsibilities:
Attract and retain talent for the Quality Engineering, Supplier Quality, Receiving Inspection teams while also supporting their development
Create a culture of quality that also ensures compliance with QMS, FDA QSR, ISO, MDR, and international requirements
Support audits and inspections by regulatory agencies and notified bodies
Drive process validation, test method development, statistical analysis, and improvement projects
Strategically drive collaboration with CAPAs, non-conformances, and risk management activities that also focus on process improvement
Use high level judgement regarding prioritization decisions, and tradeoffs between schedule, scope, and cost
Partner with R&D, Maintenance, Operations, Quality Assurance and other functions to drive prompt resolution and prioritization of tasks around quality issues for product and processes while also driving the highest quality results
Lead the oversight and influence the nonconformance system (product and non-product related) in a timely manner and serves as an activist and mentor in problem solving and root causing activities
Proactively drive and mentor continuous improvement activities to ensure problems are prevented and issued resolved efficiently and economically
Qualifications:
Bachelors degree required in a sciences or technical area relevant to the medical device industry.
Minimum of 7 years of medical device industry experience.
Minimum of 5 years of Management experience.
Extensive knowledge and experience with government regulations to assure development of Quality Systems conforming to relevant regulations.
Extensive knowledge of the requirements for international quality systems, including ISO-9001/EN 46001, ISO 13485, MDR, Vigilance Systems, Notified Bodies, CE marking and IEC 60601.
Demonstrated collaboration, team building, negotiation & conflict resolution skills
Knowledge of and working experience with Corrective Action / Preventive Action (CAPA)
Knowledge of and working experience with Supplier Management (Supplier selection / assessments /monitoring / audits / metrics)
Demonstrated knowledge of and working experience with Risk Management (ISO 14971, FMEAs, FMECAs, Hazard Analysis)
Multi-tasks, prioritizes and meets deadlines in timely manner. Strong organizational, planning, and follow-up skills and ability to hold others accountable.
Language & Verbal Skills
Strong verbal and written communications with ability to effectively communicate at multiple levels in the organization
Ability to clearly and concisely convey project accomplishments, obstacles, issues, and project status
Ability to read, analyze, and interpret engineering specifications, general business periodicals, professional journals, technical procedures, or governmental regulations
Ability to write reports, specifications, business correspondence, and procedure manuals
Analytical & Reading Skills
Exceptional analytical, problem solving & root-cause analysis skills. Ability to multitask, define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions.
Demonstrated ability interpreting a variety of technical instructions in mathematical or diagram form and deal with several abstract and concrete variables.
Ability to read technical and clinical literature and documents and extract important concepts.
Physical Requirements
May be required to perform lifting tasks of up to 30 pounds for short durations.
Duties of this job may involve standing and/or walking for extended periods of time.
Duties also involve daily keyboard data entry. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision.
Limited travel (0-10%).
Work Environment
Most work will be performed in an office environment.
The noise level in the work environment is usually low to moderate.
Safety
Solta Medical is committed to the health and safety of our employees.
We expect that all employees will perform their responsibilities while maintaining a safe, cooperative, and productive work environment, thus ensuring the health and safety of themselves and others.
The range of starting base pay for this role is$145,705 - $200,345. Actual starting pay will be based on a wide range of factors including, but not limited to, relevant skills, experience, qualifications, education and location. In addition to base pay, this position is eligible for participation in either (i) our annual bonus program or (ii) a sales incentive plan.
Benefits package includes a comprehensive Medical (includes Prescription Drug), Dental, Vision, Flexible Spending Accounts, 401(k) with matching company contribution, discretionary time off, paid sick time, stock purchase plan, tuition reimbursement, parental leave, short-term and long-term disability, life insurance, accidental death & dismemberment insurance, paid holidays, employee referral bonuses and employee discounts.
We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to building diverse teams, representative of the patients and communities we serve, and we strive to create an inclusive workplace that cultivates collaboration.

Responsibilities 
 Howmet Aerospace , headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, is a leading global provider of advanced engineered solutions for the aerospace and transportation industries. The Company’s primary businesses focus on jet engine components, aerospace fastening systems and titanium structural parts necessary for mission-critical performance and efficiency in aerospace and defense applications, as well as forged wheels for commercial transportation. Howmet Aerospace is transforming the next phase of more fuel-efficient, quieter aerospace engines and sustainable ground transportation. For more information, visit  www.howmet.com . Follow @howmet: Twitter, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn and YouTube.
 Howmet Engine Systems is currently seeking an experienced professional to join our team in Hampton, Virginia.    Are you an empowered partner with the drive to transform ideas into sustainable value?Weare seeking individuals who have a demonstrated ability to achieve results in a manufacturing environment, as well as the passion to put that experience to work to lead activities and support plant/location team to achieve manufacturing excellence.  Our organization is dedicated to rapid, profitable growth through operational excellence and career development.  If you are an energetic professional that wants to be a part of a dynamic team we encourage you to apply.  
 Job Summary: Coordinate work activities on a daily (shift to shift) basis to meet customer delivery schedules under the direction of Department Supervisor.
 Salary: 
  Anticipated Pay Range: $65K-75K per year.   *Pay rates within this range are determined based on various factors including experience, education, certifications, etc.

 Production Skills 20% 
 Coordinates workflow through department on a daily basis to meet production schedule.
 Ensures daily production goals are met in both quantity and quality.
 Utilizes production methods that reduce cost and increase productivity.
 Observes and adheres to standards of performance, identifies and reports shortfalls to supervisor.
 Ensures maintenance of equipment by application of TPM or other methods.
 Leadership 30% 
 Upholds and demonstrates Howmet’s values in approach to work, decision making and interpretations of ethical guidelines and polices for subordinates.
 Maintains relationships with peers, subordinates, superiors, external and internal customers, promotes teamwork within and between departments.
 Accepts and seeks individual/self-developmental opportunities.
 Works on assigned projects to meet department goals and objectives.
 Communications 15% 
 Communicates verbally and in writing to peers, superiors, internal and external customers and suppliers.
 Maintains communication during shift turnover through the use of turnover sheets, updated status boards or other verbal and written means.
 Make and receives verbal and written assignments.
 Conduct meetings with team members.

 Working knowledge of all non-certified operations in department.

 This position entails access to export-controlled items you must be able to lawfully obtain access to such items.

 About us

 If a pay range is identified for this job, it is based on a good faith estimate at the time of this posting. Actual compensation is subject to variation due to factors such as education, experience, skillset, market/business considerations, and/or location.

Job Overview Site Support & Internal Audits provides rapid, hands-on technical quality support for product, process, equipment, workmanship, and customer-quality issues. This role works directly with site personnel to understand problems at the source, contain risk, support root-cause analysis, coordinate or perform approved repair and rework activity, verify that corrective actions are effective, and drive sustainable process improvements.  When not responding to an active quality issue, the Quality Technician conducts internal quality-system, process, product, and layered process audits; supports corrective-action closure; evaluates adherence to standard work and quality requirements; and identifies opportunities to strengthen manufacturing controls at the site.  The successful candidate combines strong manufacturing troubleshooting ability with disciplined problem-solving, sound technical judgment, practical repair knowledge, effective communication, and the ability to work collaboratively with site teams. A Day In The Life Problem Response and Technical Diagnosis 
 • Respond to quality escalations, production disruptions, repeat defects, customer complaints, product returns, and significant nonconformances at the manufacturing site. 
 • Respond promptly at the site and assess the condition, scope, urgency, customer impact, safety implications, and production impact of the issue. 
 • Establish immediate containment actions to prevent further production, shipment, use, or installation of suspect material. 
 • Determine whether the issue is related to product design, material, supplier quality, fabrication, assembly, welding, coating, machining, wiring, testing, packaging, handling, maintenance, operator technique, inspection method, process control, or adherence to standard work. 
 • Apply structured problem-solving methods such as 5 Why, Fishbone/Ishikawa, Is/Is Not analysis, Pareto analysis, process mapping, fault-tree analysis, DOE, SPC, and 8D or corrective-action methodologies, as appropriate. 
 • Define and communicate a clear technical problem statement, including what failed, where it occurred, when it began, which product or process is affected, the extent of exposure, and the immediate next steps. 
 • Evaluate product against drawings, specifications, workmanship standards, test requirements, regulatory requirements, and customer expectations. 
 • Collect, preserve, and document objective evidence, including photographs, measurements, samples, inspection records, process parameters, repair records, and relevant traceability information. 
 Repair Assessment and Disposition 
 • Evaluate nonconforming material and equipment to determine whether it can be safely and acceptably repaired, reworked, reprocessed, used as-is through formal approval, returned to a supplier, sent to an approved outside repair source, scrapped, or replaced. 
 Quality Technician - Site Quality Support & Internal Audits 
 • Develop or review rework instructions that clearly define the defect, repair method, required tools/materials, acceptance criteria, inspection points, safety requirements, and authorization needed before release. 
 • Perform limited hands-on troubleshooting, inspection, rework, or repair activities when within the individual’s demonstrated technical competency, site authorization, safety requirements, and company procedures. 
 • Coordinate with maintenance, manufacturing engineering, product engineering, production, suppliers, and qualified external service or repair vendors when specialized repairs, equipment support, testing, calibration, machining, welding, coating, electrical work, or other technical services are required. 
 • Identify the appropriate internal function, supplier, OEM, or qualified repair vendor for work that cannot or should not be completed internally at the site. 
 • Ensure outsourced repair work is supported by clear technical requirements, documented disposition, traceability, inspection criteria, and verification before product or equipment is returned to service or released. 
 • Verify repair effectiveness through inspection, functional testing, first-piece validation, capability review, trial production, or other appropriate acceptance methods. What will help you thrive in this role? Associate degree preferred.

About Us
Our site runs a food safety management system built to the SQF Food Safety Code (Edition 9). To learn more about us, visit www.cartonservice.com.

Reporting to the President, the QA Director leads quality assurance across all our carton production. What You'll Do
• Lead and develop the QA team and oversee the plant quality system
• Review and approve customer specs, and make sure CSI procedures are followed

• Salary commensurate with experience

 Varian Medical Systems, a Siemens Healthineers company, is seeking a Senior Manager, Supplier Quality Management to lead our Supplier Quality Management organization across the Americas. In this role, you will provide strategic and operational leadership for regional Supplier Quality Management activities, ensuring the quality, reliability, and compliance of externally supplied components, materials, products, and services.
 Working closely with Procurement, Engineering, Manufacturing, Product Quality, Incoming Inspection, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, Service, and global Supplier Quality Management and Engineering partners, you will lead the Americas Supplier Quality Management team, establish regional priorities, strengthen supplier quality management governance and technical capability, and drive supplier performance and continuous improvement in alignment with the global Supplier Quality strategy.
 A key focus of this role will be advancing Quality at the Source (QATS) across the Americas, shifting quality management toward defect prevention through earlier supplier involvement, stronger supplier processes, risk-based controls, and the effective application of APQP, PPAP, SPC, process capability, FMEA, Lean, Six Sigma, and other preventive quality methodologies.
 In this role, you will mainly be responsible for the following:
 Lead, coach, and develop the Americas Supplier Quality Management organization, establishing clear objectives, priorities, responsibilities, and performance expectations while ensuring appropriate resources, competencies, and capabilities are in place.
 Provide strategic and operational leadership across the supplier quality lifecycle, including supplier selection and early involvement, qualification, onboarding, monitoring, development, NPI, Quality at the Source, product acceptance, supplier changes, quality controls, and supplier performance improvement.
 Execute the global Supplier Quality Management strategy across the Americas while contributing regional expertise, performance insights, and priorities to the continued development of global Supplier Quality processes, standards, and ways of working.
 Establish and maintain effective Supplier Quality Management governance across the Americas, ensuring consistent process execution, risk-based supplier controls, performance expectations, escalation mechanisms, and accountability.
 Ensure regional Supplier Quality activities and supplier controls comply with applicable Quality Management System and regulatory requirements, including FDA QMSR, ISO 13485:2016, ISO 14971:2019, EU MDR, and other applicable global and regional requirements.
 Lead regional implementation and execution of Quality at the Source (QATS), driving proactive defect prevention through early supplier involvement, robust manufacturing processes, risk-based controls, and integration with Incoming Inspection and Product Quality requirements. Drive the effective application of APQP, PPAP, FAI, PFMEA, Control Plans, SPC, MSA, process capability, process validation, Lean, and Six Sigma to improve supplier capability and reduce variation and defects.
 Provide governance and oversight for supplier qualification, risk assessment, supplier audits, Quality/Master/Supplier Quality Agreements, supplier changes and change notifications, ongoing supplier monitoring, and supplier development, ensuring controls and qualification requirements are appropriate to product, process, compliance, and business risk.
 Provide leadership and oversight for significant supplier nonconformances, SCARs, supplier escapes, quality escalations, and supplier development plans, ensuring timely containment, effective root cause analysis, sustainable corrective action, effectiveness verification, and appropriate escalation.
 Provide leadership during critical supplier quality events, production interruptions, field issues, and other significant supplier-related risks, ensuring timely risk mitigation, cross-functional coordination, business continuity, and sustainable resolution.
 Establish and monitor regional Supplier Quality Management performance indicators and operational metrics, integrating supplier, Incoming Inspection, manufacturing, field, warranty, nonconformance, and Cost of Poor Quality data to identify systemic trends and emerging risks and translate them into clear priorities, actions, and escalation.
 Lead Supplier Quality Management involvement in New Product Introduction, design transfer, and supplier industrialization across the Americas, ensuring appropriate early involvement, quality planning, supplier readiness, product and process qualification, and effective transition into ongoing production.
 Partner with Procurement, R&D, Engineering, Manufacturing, Product Quality, Incoming Inspection, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, Service, and other functions to integrate Supplier Quality requirements into sourcing, NPI, manufacturing, product acceptance, field-performance evaluation, and supplier management decisions.
 Drive supplier development, standardization, simplification, digitalization, and continuous improvement across the region, prioritizing initiatives based on supplier performance, product and compliance risk, business impact, Cost of Poor Quality, and supplier capability.
 Build strong relationships with strategic suppliers and engage supplier leadership as appropriate to drive accountability, resolve significant quality issues, strengthen manufacturing and quality capability, and improve long-term supplier performance.
 Develop the technical and leadership capability of the Americas Supplier Quality Management organization through coaching, competency development, knowledge sharing, and succession planning, ensuring the team has the skills required to effectively manage complex supplier and manufacturing quality risks.
 Promote a culture of quality, prevention, accountability, collaboration, technical excellence, and continuous improvement across the Americas Supplier Quality organization and supplier network.
 Minimum Required Skills and Knowledge
 Strong leadership and influencing skills, with demonstrated ability to build effective, trust-based relationships with direct reports, peers, senior leadership, cross-functional partners, and suppliers.
 Demonstrated experience leading Supplier Quality teams across multiple sites or a regional organization, including operating effectively within global and matrixed environments.
 Strong knowledge of Supplier Quality Management requirements and practices within medical devices or another highly regulated or quality-critical manufacturing environment, including supplier qualification, monitoring, auditing, development, change management, and quality escalation.
 Strong working knowledge of applicable Quality Management System and regulatory requirements, including FDA QMSR, ISO 13485:2016, ISO 14971:2019, EU MDR, MDSAP, and applicable GMP requirements.
 Strong technical understanding of supplier and manufacturing quality methods, including APQP, PPAP, FAI, PFMEA/FMEA, Control Plans, SPC, MSA/Gauge R&R, process capability (Cpk/Ppk), process validation, root cause analysis, and corrective and preventive action.
 Demonstrated technical understanding of engineering drawings, specifications, tolerances, critical characteristics, manufacturing processes, inspection requirements, and process qualification, with the ability to provide direction and coaching on complex supplier quality issues.
 Experience leading supplier audits, supplier quality escalations, complex corrective actions, SCARs, and supplier development programs, including rapid containment and risk mitigation where production, customers, or patients may be impacted.
 Strong understanding of manufacturing, supply chain, Product Quality, Incoming Inspection, and supplier operations, including their impact on product lifecycle quality and business performance.
 Proven experience in project and change management, process excellence, organizational development, and cross-functional improvement initiatives.
 Demonstrated ability to identify systemic improvement opportunities, benchmark performance and practices, establish improvement priorities, and drive sustainable change across multiple sites and functions.
 Strong business acumen and data-driven decision-making skills, with the ability to connect supplier quality performance and risk with product quality, manufacturing performance, field performance, supply continuity, compliance, and Cost of Poor Quality.
 Strong communication and executive presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex technical, quality, and supplier issues into clear risks, priorities, decisions, and calls to action for technical and non-technical stakeholders.
 Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and significant supplier escalations with appropriate independence, judgment, urgency, and accountability.
 Ability to travel up to 50%, including domestic and international supplier locations.
 Typical Education and Experience
 Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Manufacturing, Materials Engineering, or another related technical field, or equivalent relevant experience.
 5+ years of progressive leadership experience managing technical teams within Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Quality, Supply Chain, Engineering, or a related technical function.
 Demonstrated progressive people leadership experience, including hiring, developing, coaching, retaining, and leading high-performing technical teams across multiple locations.
 Experience establishing measurable objectives, performance expectations, priorities, and accountability, and effectively delegating responsibilities across direct and matrixed organizations.
 Demonstrated ability to lead significant cross-functional and multi-site Supplier Quality or process improvement initiatives, influence senior stakeholders, and drive alignment around strategic and operational priorities.
 Strong business acumen with working knowledge of Supplier Quality, Product Quality, Incoming Inspection, Procurement, Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Finance, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, and Service and their interdependencies.
 Experience establishing and using Supplier Quality KPIs, scorecards, dashboards, trend analysis, and data-based performance reviews to drive priorities, escalation, supplier development, and decision-making.
 Experience with ERP, MES, eQMS, and data analytics/reporting tools, preferably including SAP/SAP HANA, Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Power BI, Tableau, QlikView, Minitab, JMP, or similar platforms.
 Preferred Qualifications
 Significant Supplier Quality or manufacturing quality experience in the medical device, automotive, aerospace, semiconductor, electronics, or another highly regulated or quality-critical manufacturing industry.
 Experience leading a regional or multi-site Supplier Quality organization and collaborating across global teams to drive consistent processes, governance, and performance.
 Demonstrated experience establishing or scaling Quality at the Source, APQP, PPAP, supplier development, or similar preventive supplier quality programs.
 Experience supporting quality across the complete product lifecycle, including NPI, design transfer, supplier qualification, production ramp-up, manufacturing, product changes, field performance, and ongoing production.
 Experience driving reductions in supplier defects, nonconformance, scrap, rework, warranty impact, and Cost of Poor Quality through supplier capability and process improvement.
 ISO 13485:2016 Lead Auditor certification preferred, with demonstrated experience conducting or leading supplier, process, and Quality Management System audits.
 ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt, Lean certification, or equivalent professional certification preferred.
 What Will Set You Apart
 Proven leadership of regional Supplier Quality operations, balancing supplier performance, regulatory compliance, product quality, supply continuity, business priorities, and continuous improvement.
 Demonstrated ability to build and develop technically strong, high-performing Supplier Quality teams and drive accountability across geographically dispersed and matrixed organizations.
 Strong technical credibility in supplier manufacturing processes, APQP/PPAP, process controls, supplier audits, root cause analysis, and supplier development, with the ability to coach and challenge experienced Supplier Quality professionals.
 Demonstrated success advancing supplier quality from downstream inspection and defect detection toward Quality at the Source, process control, and defect prevention.
 Experience leading through high-impact supplier quality events, balancing speed of containment and business continuity with quality-system discipline, evidence-based root cause analysis, and sustainable corrective action.
 The ability to connect supplier quality performance with Incoming Inspection, manufacturing, field performance, warranty, supply continuity, regulatory compliance, and Cost of Poor Quality.
 A practical, risk-based, and data-driven leadership approach that translates complex supplier issues into clear priorities, ownership, escalation, and sustainable improvement.
 Demonstrated ability to influence senior internal stakeholders and supplier leadership, resolve complex cross-functional issues, and drive organizational change.
 A continuous improvement mindset focused on strengthening supplier capability, preventing recurrence, reducing Cost of Poor Quality, and improving the overall maturity and effectiveness of Supplier Quality Management.

Breaking beauty boundaries is in our company’s DNA.
