This role is an Onsite Role: This role requires full-time presence at our Oxford, NC office.
Overview
Responsible for the safe and efficient operation of the Oxford Filling and Assembly operation – may include multiple cost centers (or all). Specific responsibilities include Ensuring that the workplace is safe, and employees work in a safe manner; Provide that all GMP requirements and regulations are complied with; Ensuring that all people issues and developmental needs are met; monitoring production requirements such that all customer needs are met on a timely basis; Responsible for all financial results of the operation.
Act as a backup to the Vice President of Manufacturing (as needed) and the Oxford site General Manager (as needed). Be aware of any major issues/action underway in other cost centers / production areas in order to fill in as needed.
Responsibilities
Safety: Ensure that a safe workplace is maintained at all times. Provide resources necessary to be proactive towards addressing issues in the workplace. Comply with all OSHA & Revlon guidelines and procedures. Assist Safety Director as needed with task forces, projects and teams. Measures: Safety incident rate; OSHA & Workmen’s comp rates; Revlon Safety Index.
People: Strive to make the Oxford site a great place to work by: proactively developing people (cross training, class work and challenges); Addressing all issues, concerns and disciplinary actions promptly and effectively; contributing to site efforts to address issues and concerns. Measures: GPTW survey results; Developmental activity; providing challenges & changes to drive the organization forward.
GMP / Regulatory: Ensure that all Revlon & Governmental Good Manufacturing Practices are complied with. Provide resources necessary to address any issues before the operation is adversely affected. Work with the site Quality Director (and others – as needed) to implement any new requirements due to new products or new regulations. Provide / facilitate training as needed. Ensure that all appropriate records are accurate and maintained within guidelines. Measures: First pass yields, rejection rates (domestic and international); GMP audit scores.
Customer Service: Ensure that all Customer requirements (domestic, international & special markets) are met per company objectives (Regular business forecast & Promotional commitments). Evaluate production needs on a forward basis to ensure that needed equipment and people resources are available to meet the customer’s needs. Measures: Schedule adherence; % Dollars shipped vs. ordered (CSL); performance to promotional ship on time commitments.
Financial: Responsible for all financial aspects of the Filling and Assembly operation: Control of Labor – Direct (productive effort); Indirect (support effort); Nonstandard (Rework & First pass yield issues); Material – performance to established standards & minimization of waste; Overhead – effective utilization of management staff, supplies and ancillary equipment; Capital – effective, proactive utilization of installed equipment base, addressing capacity and new product needs with adequate lead time to meet customer’s needs. Support and facilitate site cost reduction objectives. Measures: Labor – Direct efficiency, indirect % to earned, nonstandard % to earned; Material – MUV; Overhead – performance to budget & tasks.
Overhead – Supplies, executive staff, support labor – Up to $14 Million annually
Material – Value of material moved through the filling and assembly operation - $250 Million annually
Labor – Direct Labor managed in the filling and assembly operation - $30 Million annually
Responsible For Establishing Processes To
Ensure that all employees in the operation have defined job duties and expectations and are managed according to those duties – and that timely corrective action takes place when needed.
Ensure that reasonable schedules are formulated, meeting customer’s needs and equipment capability. Interface with appropriate departments as needed to affect change.
Ensure that all equipment is operational and performs within expected tolerances.
Ensure that all Revlon and governmental policies, guidelines, rules and procedures are followed and adhered to.
Interface with all other sites functional areas as needed (HR, Quality, Distribution, Finance, etc.)
Qualifications
Extensive knowledge of production equipment, especially safe operating techniques, product capabilities and trouble-shooting methods
Knowledge of planning / scheduling forecasting processes and systems
Knowledge and experience with operations in an FDA – GMP environment
Significant communication skills – verbal and written
High level ability to analyze situations, and ability to facilitate cross functional teams
Demonstrated success in people development and driving an organization forward
Basic computer skills including Excel, Word, and use of MRP systems
Prefer a 4-year degree in an engineering discipline, but other areas of study will be considered with appropriate and relevant experience
Minimum 15 years of experience required
Ability to make decisions
Ability to effectively set and enforce company policy affecting up to 2,500 employees – communicate changes and issues to said group
Significant operating knowledge of the Cosmetic industry – products, equipment and business practices
Knowledge of Customer / Supplier relationships and how to best manage those to get results
Shift hours: 8:00am - 5:00pm

This is not a corporate executive role designed to lead from a conference room.
 

 We are looking for a proven change agent who is equally comfortable reviewing financial results, leading daily operational reviews, solving production challenges on the shop floor, and developing frontline leaders.
 

 This is a multi-site position, initially focused on Jensen Metal Products and Jensen Powder Finishers. The successful candidate will build the structure, discipline, and performance culture needed to support long-term growth across KSP Group.
 

 The ideal candidate brings deep experience in fabrication and manufacturing environments, a strong operational and financial mindset, and a proven ability to lead teams through growth and transformation.
 

 About KSP Group 
 KSP Group is a family-owned organization with a diverse portfolio of manufacturing and consumer product companies
 

 Jensen Metal Products – Custom metal fabrication, welding, machining, laser cutting, engineering and contract manufacturing solutions (Racine, WI)
 Jensen Powder Finishers – Advanced powder coating and finishing services (Sturtevant, WI) 
 Jensen Castings – Manufacturer of premium GFRC concrete fire features (Richland Center, WI) 
 Real Flame – A leading designer and manufacturer of fireplaces, fire tables, and outdoor living products sold through major retailers across North America (Union Grove, WI) 
 

 Together, our companies are built on innovation, craftsmanship, customer partnerships, and a commitment to continuous improvement.
 

 Here, you'll have the opportunity to make a visible impact, influence company strategy, and help shape the future of multiple growing businesses.
 

 

 What You'll Do 
 Executive Strategic & Business Leadership

 Identify opportunities for automation, process optimization, capacity expansion, and operational scalability
 Financial & Operational Performance
 Own operational performance and P&L results across assigned manufacturing operations
 Develop departmental budgets, monitor spending, and ensure responsible management of operational resources
 Analyze manufacturing costs, labor efficiency, productivity metrics, and operating expenses to drive profitability
 Report on operational performance and improvement initiatives to executive leadership
 Manufacturing Operations & Continuous Improvement
 Lead continuous improvement initiatives across fabrication, welding, machining, powder coating, assembly, engineering, and support functions
 Drive Lean Manufacturing, Kaizen, 5S, root cause problem solving, and waste reduction efforts
 Improve throughput, quality, safety, delivery performance, and overall operational efficiency
 Lead cross-functional projects focused on sustainable operational gains and measurable business results
 Leadership & Culture
 Build, coach, and develop high-performing operational leadership teams
 Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement
 Promote employee engagement while creating a safe, quality-focused work environment
 

 Requirements

 Demonstrated success leading directly from the manufacturing floor, including personal involvement in:

 Corrective action processes
 Maintenance and equipment planning
 Capital investment justification
 Safety and operational accountability
 Frontline leadership development
 Proven track record of transforming entrepreneurial manufacturing organizations into process-driven, scalable operations through both strategic leadership and active engagement with frontline teams
 Ability to establish accountability without creating unnecessary bureaucracy

 Preferred Qualifications

 Experience within both contract manufacturing and consumer products environments

 Travel Requirements

 About Us 
 Jensen Metal Products is a metal fabrication business with over 100 years of experience serving the Midwest and surrounding regions with custom, quality sheet metal parts and assemblies. With a broad range of manufacturing capabilities, we produce a diverse portfolio of products, including our own line of fireplaces, which has been in production since 1970. We serve many types of businesses including the agricultural, retail, energy and healthcare fields. From engineering to packaging, our goal is to be a one-stop shop that exceeds our customers’ expectations for quality, delivery, great customer service and cost. At Jensen Metal Products we pride ourselves on having strong, long-lasting relationships with our employees and customers. We welcome you to join our team!

Overview

 ServiceLink is seeking an experienced Director of Quality Engineering and Automation to lead our quality engineering transformation. This leader will be responsible for defining and executing the enterprise quality strategy, modernizing test automation capabilities, establishing quality governance standards, and driving engineering-wide quality improvements.

 

 This role is not a traditional QA management position focused solely on test execution. The Director will serve as the organization’s quality engineering leader, responsible for building scalable automation capabilities, establishing meaningful quality metrics, and influencing software quality outcomes across Engineering, Product, and Release organizations.

 

 The ideal candidate combines deep quality engineering expertise with strong organizational leadership, executive communication skills, and a proven ability to drive meaningful change in highly matrixed environments. Success in this role requires the ability to influence decisions through data, credibility, partnership, and quality leadership rather than direct organizational authority.

 

 ServiceLink is modernizing the mortgage services industry through AI-accelerated engineering, intelligent automation, and next-generation software delivery practices. We empower the nation’s top lenders and financial institutions with advanced technology, data-driven insights, and high-velocity product development models.

 

 As we continue to scale our technology platforms, we are investing in a modern Quality Engineering organization focused on automation, quality governance, engineering excellence, and continuous delivery. Our goal is to transform quality from a downstream testing activity into an engineering capability embedded throughout the software development lifecycle.

 

 This is a hybrid role, and will be required to work in-office at our Plano, TX office at least 3 days per week. Candidates must be located within reasonable commuting distance of this office and be willing to work in-office on a regular basis. 

 

 Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis and must not require sponsorship for employment visa status now or in the future. 

 

 A DAY IN THE LIFE

 In this role, you will…

 

 · Lead quality engineering transformation

 · Own enterprise test automation strategy

 · Establish quality governance and risk management policies and procedures

 · Drive engineering quality excellence

 · Influence cross-functional release and product outcomes

 · Establish quality metrics and executive reporting

 · Lead and develop the Quality Engineering organization

 

 Success Measures

 · Automated coverage of critical business workflows.

 · Reduction in manual regression testing effort.

 · Improved release predictability and confidence.

 · Reduction in escaped production defects.

 · Increased adoption of shift-left quality practices.

 · Expanded developer ownership of quality.

 · Enhanced visibility into quality trends and release readiness risks.

 · Increased executive confidence in quality governance and software delivery outcomes.

 

 

 WHO YOU ARE

 You possess …

 

 · 10+ years of progressive experience in software quality, quality engineering, software engineering, or related technology leadership roles.

 · 5+ years of experience leading quality engineering organizations in complex enterprise software environments.

 · Demonstrated success leading large-scale test automation and quality transformation initiatives.

 · Experience building and scaling automation frameworks and engineering quality practices.

 · Strong understanding of modern SDLC practices, CI/CD pipelines, DevOps, and cloud-native application architectures.

 · Experience implementing API, integration, end-to-end, performance, and regression testing strategies.

 · Demonstrated ability to influence executive stakeholders and lead cross-functional initiatives without direct authority.

 · Experience establishing quality metrics, executive scorecards, and data-driven governance models.

 · Strong understanding of risk management, release readiness, and quality governance practices.

 · Experience managing distributed teams and complex organizational change efforts.

 · Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to engage technical and business audiences.

 · Experience leveraging AI-assisted engineering and testing tools such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, or similar technologies.

 Responsibilities

 1. Lead Quality Engineering Transformation

 • Define and execute a multi-year quality engineering strategy aligned with ServiceLink’s technology and business objectives.

 • Transform the organization from a predominantly manual testing model to an automation-first quality engineering approach.

 • Establish scalable operating models, standards, and best practices across quality engineering functions.

 • Evaluate and implement AI-assisted testing capabilities where they provide measurable business value.

 • Continuously improve testing effectiveness, release confidence, and overall software quality.

 • Develop a strategic roadmap that reduces manual regression testing effort while improving coverage and reliability.

 

 2. Own Enterprise Test Automation Strategy

 • Define and execute automation strategies spanning unit, API, integration, end-to-end, performance, and regression testing.

 • Build and maintain modern automation frameworks supporting multiple product portfolios and technology stacks.

 • Identify opportunities to automate repetitive testing activities and reduce release-cycle effort.

 • Establish automation standards, coding practices, and framework governance.

 • Drive automation adoption across engineering teams and development pipelines.

 • Ensure automation investments directly support business outcomes through measurable reductions in manual testing effort

 and improved release quality.

 

 3. Establish Quality Governance and Risk Management

 • Define enterprise quality standards, testing policies, and release readiness criteria.

 • Develop risk-based testing frameworks that focus resources on the highest-value business scenarios.

 • Provide objective assessments of release readiness and software quality risks.

 • Establish processes for identifying, documenting, communicating, and escalating quality concerns.

 • Lead post-release reviews and quality retrospectives to identify systemic improvement opportunities.

 • Create clear mechanisms for risk visibility and executive decision support.

 

 4. Drive Engineering Quality Excellence

 • Partner with software engineering leaders to embed quality throughout the SDLC.

 • Champion shift-left testing practices and developer ownership of quality.

 • Promote increased use of automated testing within CI/CD pipelines.

 • Drive adoption of engineering practices that improve code quality, testability, maintainability, and system reliability.

 • Collaborate with architecture and development teams to improve overall product quality and reduce defect introduction

 rates.

 • Influence engineering decisions through quality metrics, technical insights, and continuous improvement recommendations.

 

 5. Influence Cross-Functional Release and Product Outcomes

 • Build strong working relationships across Product Management, Release Management, Engineering, Operations, and

 Support organizations.

 • Serve as a trusted advisor on quality, testing strategy, release readiness, and operational risk.

 • Influence planning, prioritization, and release decisions through data-driven recommendations and quality insights.

 • Ensure stakeholders understand the quality implications of scope changes, late-stage modifications, and release decisions.

 • Foster organizational alignment around quality objectives and customer experience outcomes.

 • Facilitate constructive discussions regarding risk, readiness, and delivery trade-offs.

 

 6. Establish Quality Metrics and Executive Reporting

 • Define and maintain enterprise quality KPIs and executive dashboards.

 • Track and communicate trends related to:

 o Escaped defects

 o Automation coverage

 o Regression testing effort

 o Test effectiveness

 o Production incidents

 o Release quality

 o Customer-impacting defects

 • Use quantitative analysis to identify improvement opportunities and support investment decisions.

 • Provide executive leadership with clear visibility into quality trends, risks, and organizational progress.

 

 7. Lead and Develop the Quality Engineering Organization

 • Build, mentor, and develop high-performing quality engineering teams.

 • Create career paths for automation engineers, quality engineers, and quality leaders.

 • Attract and retain top quality engineering talent.

 • Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, continuous learning, and operational excellence.

 • Ensure organizational structures support both immediate delivery needs and long-term quality transformation goals.

 Qualifications

 Required

 · 10+ years of progressive experience in software quality, quality engineering, software engineering, or related technology leadership roles.

 · 5+ years of experience leading quality engineering organizations in complex enterprise software environments.

 · Demonstrated success leading large-scale test automation and quality transformation initiatives.

 · Experience building and scaling automation frameworks and engineering quality practices.

 · Strong understanding of modern SDLC practices, CI/CD pipelines, DevOps, and cloud-native application architectures.

 · Experience implementing API, integration, end-to-end, performance, and regression testing strategies.

 · Demonstrated ability to influence executive stakeholders and lead cross-functional initiatives without direct authority.

 · Experience establishing quality metrics, executive scorecards, and data-driven governance models.

 · Strong understanding of risk management, release readiness, and quality governance practices.

 · Experience managing distributed teams and complex organizational change efforts.

 · Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to engage technical and business audiences.

 · Experience leveraging AI-assisted engineering and testing tools such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, or similar technologies.

 

 Preferred

 · Experience leading quality engineering organizations undergoing significant automation transformation.

 · Background in highly regulated industries such as financial services, mortgage, banking, insurance, healthcare, or fintech.

 · Experience implementing quality engineering practices within Agile and product-oriented delivery models.

 · Knowledge of modern test automation platforms, quality engineering frameworks, and observability tools.

 · Experience supporting large-scale digital transformation initiatives.

Overview
Englert - Director of Manufacturing
As the Director of Manufacturing, you will lead daily operations and drives sustained performance across Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, and People. Reporting to the President of Manufacturing, this role partners with Quality, Maintenance, Engineering/Continuous Improvement, Supply Chain, Production Planning, and other support functions to achieve plant objectives.
This leader is accountable for production performance, labor productivity, schedule attainment, manufacturing cost, capacity utilization, talent development, and continuous improvement. The role establishes disciplined shop-floor management, develops manufacturing leaders, and builds a culture of accountability, problem solving, teamwork, and operational excellence.
Pay Range: Starting at $130,000 per year with variable comp
Responsibilities
Lead daily manufacturing operations to meet or exceed targets for Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Productivity, and People.
Convert forecasts, demand, and business priorities into manufacturing plans, staffing models, capacity requirements, and execution priorities.
Lead, coach, and develop manufacturing managers, supervisors, and frontline leaders with clear expectations, accountability, and performance standards.
Maintain a disciplined daily management system with shift meetings, production reviews, KPI boards, escalation routines, and corrective-action follow-up.
Monitor manufacturing KPIs including safety performance, schedule attainment, output, labor efficiency, overtime, scrap, rework, downtime, productivity, and manufacturing cost.
Ensure production issues and performance gaps are quickly identified, root causes addressed, corrective actions assigned, and results sustained.
Partner with Quality to improve first-pass yield, reduce defects and rework, resolve customer concerns, and strengthen process controls.
Partner with Maintenance to improve equipment reliability, reduce unplanned downtime, strengthen preventive maintenance, and increase asset utilization.
Collaborate with Production Planning and Supply Chain to align schedules, material availability, inventory needs, and customer commitments.
Partner with Engineering and Continuous Improvement to improve productivity, capacity, material flow, ergonomics, quality, and manufacturing cost.
Drive Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement through standard work, 5S/6S, visual management, problem solving, waste elimination, line balancing, and process optimization.
Increase output and capacity utilization while reducing labor hours, overtime, scrap, rework, downtime, and operational waste.
Establish, document, train, audit, and sustain standardized work processes and operating procedures.
Develop capacity and labor plans that support current demand, growth initiatives, new products, and changing customer requirements.
Use ERP systems and operational data to analyze performance, identify trends, set priorities, and drive factbased decisions.
Maintain daily, weekly, and monthly reporting that compares results to targets and highlights trends, gaps, and corrective actions.
Support the annual operating plan, manufacturing budget, capital requirements, productivity initiatives, and cost-reduction targets.
Manage manufacturing expenses within budget and deliver year-over-year improvements in labor productivity, conversion cost, scrap, and operational efficiency.
Champion safety by ensuring compliance with standards, participation in safety initiatives, and proactive risk identification and elimination.
Ensure manufacturing operations comply with company policies, regulatory requirements, quality systems, environmental requirements, and operating procedures.
Build succession plans and strengthen the leadership pipeline through coaching, performance management, cross-training, and talent development.
Partner with Human Resources to support hiring, onboarding, training, and retention of manufacturing employees and leaders.
Foster a culture where employees identify problems, recommend improvements, and engage in continuous improvement.
Perform other duties and lead special projects as assigned by the Sr. Director of Manufacturing Operations.
Qualifications
Key Performance Indicators
Success Will Be Measured By Sustained Improvement In
Safety performance
First-pass yield and internal quality
Customer quality and manufacturing-related complaints
Schedule attainment and on-time completion
Labor productivity and efficiency
Overtime
Scrap and rework
Equipment downtime and capacity utilization
Manufacturing cost
Inventory and material flow
Continuous improvement savings
Employee development, engagement, and retention

Manufacturing Leadership: Proven ability to lead complex manufacturing operations and deliver results through execution, accountability, and disciplined follow-through.
Operational Excellence: Strong command of manufacturing systems, production management, standard work, capacity planning, labor optimization, and performance management.
Lean Manufacturing & Continuous Improvement: Ability to apply Lean principles and structured problem solving to eliminate waste, improve flow, increase productivity, and reduce cost.
Financial Acumen: Strong understanding of manufacturing cost, labor performance, budgeting, productivity, capital investment, and plant profitability drivers.
Data-Driven Decision Making: Ability to use ERP systems, KPIs, dashboards, and financial data to identify trends, prioritize opportunities, and drive corrective action.
People Leadership: Proven ability to coach, develop, and hold leaders accountable while building a highperformance, respectful, and collaborative culture.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Ability to work effectively with Quality, Maintenance, Supply Chain, Engineering, Continuous Improvement, Finance, Human Resources, Sales, and other partners.
Problem Solving: Strong analytical skills with demonstrated use of structured root-cause analysis and corrective-action methods.
Change Leadership: Ability to lead organizational and operational changes while building ownership and accountability across manufacturing.
Shop-Floor Leadership: Hands-on leadership style with consistent floor presence and direct engagement with employees, supervisors, and operations.
Education And Experience
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business or related field required; equivalent education and significant manufacturing leadership experience may be considered.
Minimum 7–10 years of progressive manufacturing experience, including at least five years in manufacturing leadership.
Experience managing multi-shift manufacturing operations and leading managers and supervisors.
Strong background in Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, structured problem solving, and performance management.
Experience using ERP/MRP systems and manufacturing data to manage performance and guide operational decisions.
Experience managing manufacturing budgets, labor productivity, cost reduction, and operational improvement programs.
Experience working within formal safety and quality management systems.
Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or equivalent practical continuous improvement experience preferred.

Bilingual Spanish preffered

The Director of Manufacturing must be a visible shop-floor leader who creates accountability, develops leaders, and prevents recurring operational issues.

This role works with the Sr. Director of Manufacturing Operations and leaders across Quality, Maintenance, Supply Chain, Engineering/Continuous Improvement, Finance, and Human Resources to achieve site and business objectives.

A Snapshot of Your Day 
 As the Head of Quality Management and Duty Optimization for North America within our Taxes & Customs organization, you will lead strategic initiatives to safeguard trade compliance, establish robust governance frameworks, and drive financial efficiency across customs operations in the United States and Canada. You will develop and maintain regional customs quality management frameworks aligned with the global customs strategy and Siemens Energy's Customs Internal Control Program, while overseeing duty payment reconciliation, internal reviews, and compliance governance. In this management-level role, you will lead a geographically distributed regional quality team and collaborate closely with Finance, Accounting, Controlling, customs brokers, service providers, and business stakeholders. You will also drive customs digitalization and process automation to strengthen compliance, optimize operational costs, and support business continuity across North America. 
 
 
 How You’ll Make an Impact 
 
 
 Develop, maintain, and audit the regional customs quality management and governance framework across the United States and Canada, ensuring alignment with the global customs strategy and Siemens Energy's Customs Internal Control Program. 
 Execute internal review and audit programs, including spot checks, trade compliance audits, and corrective action management, to identify, assess, and mitigate compliance risks while ensuring continuous improvement of customs processes and controls. 
 Monitor regulatory developments in North American trade laws and customs regulations, driving appropriate process and control enhancements to maintain compliance with applicable requirements. 
 Ensure timely and compliant payment and reconciliation of customs duties and broker fees in collaboration with Finance, Accounting, and Controlling functions, supporting accurate financial reporting and duty optimization. 
 Lead and manage projects focused on advancing customs process automation and digitalization to strengthen compliance, improve operational efficiency, and optimize customs-related costs. 
 Provide direct supervision, mentorship, and development to a geographically distributed regional quality team, while partnering with business stakeholders, customs brokers, service providers, and operational teams throughout North America to align customs compliance with business objectives. 
 
 
 
 What You Bring 
 
 
 Bachelor's degree in International Business, Supply Chain Management, Finance, Law, or a related field. 
 8–10 years of experience in customs, international trade compliance, or a related discipline, with significant experience supporting customs operations in the United States and Canada. 
 Extensive knowledge of North American customs regulations and compliance requirements, including tariff classification, customs valuation, country of origin, import/export controls, recordkeeping, and customs internal control frameworks. 
 Experience with trade audit methodologies, regulatory risk assessment, internal control programs, and the development and implementation of customs quality management and governance frameworks. 
 Demonstrated leadership and team management capabilities, including direct supervision, mentorship, and development of geographically distributed and cross-functional teams in a complex, multinational environment. 
 Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with senior executives, Finance, Accounting, Controlling, customs brokers, service providers, operational teams, and regulatory authorities. Experience with customs IT solutions, process automation, and digitalization initiatives is highly desirable. Licensed Customs Broker (LCB) or Certified Customs Specialist (CCS) certification is preferred. 
 Applicants must be legally authorized for employment in the United States without need for current or future employer-sponsored work authorization. Siemens Energy employees with current visa sponsorship may be eligible for internal transfers. 
 
 

 Equal Employment Opportunity Statement 

Siemens Energy and Siemens Gamesa Renewable Energy is an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to their race, color, creed, religion, national origin, citizenship status, ancestry, sex, age, physical or mental disability unrelated to ability, marital status, family responsibilities, pregnancy, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender expression, gender identity, transgender, sex stereotyping, order of protection status, protected veteran or military status, or an unfavorable discharge from military service, and other categories protected by federal, state or local law.

About Genesis
 We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.
 We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.
 
 The role
 You own the supply chain for a general-purpose robot going from prototype to production: every part in the bill of materials, from actuators, gears and motors to structures, PCBAs, harnesses, batteries and sensors, and every supplier and manufacturing partner behind them. You build it from the ground up, in the United States and abroad, and you build the team that runs it. The scale goes from tens of units to hundreds to thousands, and the supply base, partners and processes that got us to today will not be the ones that get us there. Building the next version is the job.
 This is a role for someone who has done it before, in the trenches, and wants to do it again with a product that matters more than the last one. You will spend your weeks with suppliers, on the floor with our manufacturing partners, in design reviews with the engineers who are still changing the parts, and with the leadership team on the decisions that shape the company. Strategy and execution are the same job here.
 
 Why this role
 Few people get to decide how a new category of machine gets built. Eno is dexterous, wheeled and already working with real customers, built today with a supply base and partners that got us here. The next version of that supply chain, the one that takes us to volume, is yours to shape: what we make and what we buy, where in the world it comes from, which partners we grow with, and what the robot costs at scale. Those choices will be visible in every unit we ship for years.
 
 What you'll do
 Strategy. Set the supply chain strategy from pilot to volume: make versus buy, regional footprint, domestic content for regulated markets, single versus dual source by sub-system, and the order in which each piece moves as volume grows.
 Partners. Own contract manufacturer and partner relationships at the executive level: selection, agreements, capacity commitments, cost and quality performance, and the transfer of sub-assemblies between regions and partners when the plan calls for it.
 Cost. Own the cost roadmap: should-cost and total-cost models, the path from pilot cost to target cost, tooling and capital decisions, long-term agreements with pricing that steps down with volume; partner with Finance on working capital and with Legal on supplier agreements.
 Supply base. Build the supplier base for the hard sub-systems: actuators, gears and motors, machined and cast structures, PCBAs, harnesses, shells, batteries and sensors; two qualified sources for every critical part, in the regions the product and our customers require.
 Risk. Run capacity and risk: capacity ahead of demand, lead-time and allocation strategy for constrained parts, tariff and trade exposure, geopolitical and single-point-of-failure risk, and a plan for each.
 Team. Build and lead the organization: sourcing, supplier development, planning, supplier quality and logistics. Hire the leaders under you, hold a high bar, set the operating cadence and the weekly numbers (clear-to-build, on-time delivery, purchase price variance, inventory, supplier quality) and the readout to the leadership team and the board.
 Systems. Stand up what a scaled organization runs on, with Manufacturing Engineering and Platform: part numbering, BOM and change control, MRP and ERP, supplier portal, traceability. Lightweight first, then more.
 Design. Be in the design conversation from the start: bring supplier capability and cost into the product early, and push the design toward what can be built at volume at the right price.
 
 What we are looking for
 Built it before. You have led the supply chain organization for a complex electromechanical product from first builds through production at scale, and either built the supply base from scratch or moved it to a new geography. Robotics, electric vehicles, aerospace, consumer electronics or medical devices.
 Leader of leaders. You have built a supply chain organization, hired its managers, and run it on numbers; you can still do the work yourself when the team is three people.
 Commercial weight. You have negotiated with contract manufacturers and tier-one suppliers at the executive level and closed long-term agreements that held up under pressure.
 Global. You have sourced across regions, including Asia and North America, and moved production between them.
 Cost record. You can walk through a BOM cost-down from pilot to volume part by part, and you know where the money hides.
 Technical. You read drawings and GD&T, you understand actuators, gearboxes, motors and PCBAs well enough to challenge an engineer constructively, and you are fluent in BOMs, change control, should-cost and MRP.
 Pace. You default to urgency, operate without a playbook, and are comfortable before the systems exist.
 Experience. Typically 10 or more years in supply chain, sourcing or manufacturing operations for complex hardware, with time in a mature organization so you know what good looks like at scale, and time in a company that was building it. Engineering degree preferred.
 
 What else you need to know
 On-site in the Bay Area. Travel to suppliers and partner sites, including international, up to 40%.
 
 How we work
 We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:
 Limitless ambition. We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.
 Relentless urgency . Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.
 Type-2 Fun. Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.
 Radical transparency. Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.
 Multiculturalism. We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.
 Team over ego. Help others, share context, and win as a team.
 A joyful journey. We take pride in the craft, enjoy the ride, and make space to laugh. Happiness is part of how we get there.

Netflix Animation Studios is on a mission to entertain the world with bold, immersive animated films that are timeless and impactful. We are paving the way for the future of animation by building a community of amazing artists and talent across three vibrant locations globally. Come join us!

The Opportunity:

 


The Pre-Production Technical Director is responsible for supporting creative and visual objectives through pipeline troubleshooting, user support, technical direction, and tool development for front-end craft groups, including Story, Edit, Art, Concept, Design, Visual Development, and Previs. As a technical expert, the Pre-Production Technical Director exhibits a deep understanding of processes, technology, and tools within these domains. They contribute technical expertise to the design and development of artist workflows and tools, ensuring that the pre-production process is efficient and integrated with the overall production pipeline. 

 


What You’ll Do:

 * Understand the visual requirements for productions and suggest new technologies, or design procedures, techniques, and tools to meet these requirements.

 * Contribute to the direction, evolution, and maintenance of the technology within the Pre-Production Department.

 * Track and resolve the most complex technical issues within Pre-Production in partnership with other TDs and Software Engineers.

 * Actively participate in brainstorming and problem-solving, contributing technical expertise and insight to create and maintain technology within the canonical production pipeline. 
 * Support the organization’s overall technical goals as required.

 


Bidding & Scheduling Responsibilities: 

 * Be aware of the deadlines for own development initiatives and actively engage in keeping these on track. 
 * Continuously monitor the scope of the most technically challenging development initiatives within the Pre-Production department and help to ensure scope adjustments have additional estimates, etc. 
 * Prioritize and break down technical projects into organized parts. 
 * Work with the Supervising TD to prepare estimates and pitches as required.

 


Talent & Performance Management Responsibilities: 

 * Work with the Supervising TD for Front-End to provide technical guidance to Pre-Production TDs with day-to-day issues and escalate through the right channels when necessary. 
 * Work with Technology Talent Management and Supervising TDs to help further develop the skills and abilities of mid-level TDs within the Front End Craft Group. 
 * Mentor mid-level TDs within the team and assist in orientation with senior new starters. 
 * Create synergies between different work groups to promote efficiency and optimization and to generate innovative ideas and approaches to how we do things.

 


Communication Collaboration & Relationship Development Responsibilities: 

 * Strong communication skills for technical ideas, project status, problems, requirements, rollout plans, etc. 
 * Able to communicate with Program Managers to contribute to the scheduling and planning of complex technology initiatives. 
 * Able to discuss complex issues with Senior Software Engineers, developers, and supervisors. 
 * Able to present to small teams (tool demos, Show Contract process, Support Dashboards, etc.). 
 * Good written communication skills for specs, tickets, status updates, etc.

 


Behaviours: 

 * Takes a collaborative approach, always working towards team goals and success.
 * Is artist-focused, passionate about improving the artist experience and workflow.
 * Acts as a proactive contributor, eager to learn and help the team succeed.
 * Stays supportive and approachable, fostering a friendly and open environment.
 * Is detail-oriented, ensuring high standards in all work.
 * Remains trustworthy and reliable in all responsibilities. 

 


What You’ll Need:

 * Relevant education in software engineering and/or film creation process.
 * 5+ years of proven pipeline TD experience in large-scale animated features, animated TV series, games and/or VFX feature films.
 * Proven technical achievements within feature animation or VFX.
 * An understanding of traditional techniques appropriate to the Pre-Production craft group. 
 * Comprehensive experience using and troubleshooting in relevant software such as Maya, Flix, Avid, Storyboard Pro, Premiere, Photoshop, and other related software used in the Pre-Production domain. 
 * Comprehensive understanding of technical details within the Pre-Production department. 
 * Ability to code review and troubleshoot problems as they arise. 
 * Expert knowledge in Python as well as PyQt or another GUI toolkit. 
 * Knowledge of concepts like data flow, data dependencies, metadata, publishing, and retrieval. 
 * Solid understanding of C++ is a plus. A strong understanding of USD and its general concepts. 
 * Knowledge of Flow Production Tracking (ShotGrid). 
 * Knowledge of code management software such as git and GitHub and code review processes. 
 * Knowledge of software development practices such as Agile and how to apply them in software such as Jira. 
 * Degree in Animation, Film, Computer Science, Design, Engineering, Math, or Physics, or equivalent combination of education and work experience in animation/VFX.

As a world leader in creating comfortable, sustainable, and efficient climate solutions for buildings, homes and transportation, it's our responsibility to put the planet first.  Learn about our benefits designed for you to thrive at work and at home.

procedures and controls to improve overall customer satisfaction, DPPM, first-pass yield, and warranty results.

 Strategic Capability: Proficiency in developing and implementing strategic plans and managing a complex P&L.

V2I-7635688BFAD1.text:
Overview

 Element has an opportunity for an experienced Quality Manager . Reporting to the General Manager, you are an essential member of the management team and responsible for the overall quality performance. This includes the Element quality management system (QMS), Prime approvals, improving First Time Right, maintaining and developing relationships with Aerospace Primes and customers and improving processes. The successful candidate will have a sound working knowledge of ISO/IEC 17025 and Nadcap requirements in relation to materials testing. Experience in relation to the Aerospace industry and Nadcap for NDT inspection and Materials testing would be desirable. 

 

 In this role, you will have interaction with clients, Accreditation Bodies and Primes and will be responsible for advising operational colleagues of the importance of quality, accuracy and integrity in the provision of the inspection and testing services we provide.

 

 You will be involved in leading quality at a local level and will work closely with the Division Quality Manager to ensure that Element quality policies, processes and procedures are effectively implemented in St. Paul, MN. As a quality leader within Element you will be capable of driving a culture of quality assurance and quality improvement, working closely with your operational colleagues and the wider Element quality community.

 

 Our laboratory in St. Paul operates a full materials testing laboratory with mechanical testing, metallurgical testing, advanced materials testing, Nadcap certified nondestructive testing (NDT), certified weld inspection, failure analysis and chemistry services. We are among the most trusted providers of construction materials testing services in the US.

 

 

 Responsibilities

 
 Maintenance and scope extension of all accreditations (e.g. ISO/IEC 17025 and Nadcap), Prime approvals and any other regulatory requirements 

 Implement and maintain the QMS, ensuring the necessary controls are in place to govern the inspection and testing undertaken

 Effectively manage the day to day implementation of the QMS and support colleagues in its implementation

 Prioritise activities to meet the needs of the business, colleagues and our customers

 Embed and drive a culture of quality assurance and quality improvement in all parts of the laboratory operations

 Ensure the continued fulfillment of customer expectations through the implementation of the QMS, e.g. through effective contact review, reporting and in communication with customers or approval bodies

 Ensure that all accreditations are maintained and extended, as agreed with operational management and the Division Quality Manager, to service our customer base and retrain our competitive position as a leader in materials testing

 Manage A2LA and Nadcap assessments, visits from and other regulatory bodies as required

 Ensure that any findings from assessments are responded to in line with the Element established quality requirements and in the timeline and format dictated by the assessment bodies 

 Establish and implement appropriate QA/QC programs to reduce the cost of poor quality and improve compliance to regulations, standards. company objectives and customer requirements

 Ensure training in the electronic quality management system (eQMS) is effective and that colleagues implement the system across the facility

 Drive and monitor the implementation of eQMS in Monterrey ensuring full usage of the available modules

 Provide quality training to colleagues when onboarding and provide refresher training to existing colleagues

 Implement method audits, system audits, and proficiency testing in line with the established schedule(s) and ensure these are maintained up to date

 Maintain good working relationships with operational colleagues within Monterrey and with the wider quality community

 
 Skills / Qualifications

 
 Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent qualification) in a scientific or engineering discipline, with ideally 5 years’ experience in materials testing or a related environment (e.g. manufacturing)

 Experience of working in an ISO / IEC 17025 environment is a prerequisite

 Nadcap experience would be preferred

 Effective organizational and time management skills with the ability prioritize activities

 Excellent communication skills

 Experience in participating in quality investigations, undertaking root cause analysis, developing corrective action plans, and ensuring the effectiveness of actions undertaken

 Requirement to keep up to date with changes in the quality landscape and maintain personal professional development

 Ability to identify quality and technical problems and work with colleagues to determine effective and sustainable solutions

 Ability to collaborate with colleagues and work effectively as part of a team

 
 Company Overview

 Element is one of the fastest growing testing, inspection and certification businesses in the world. Globally we have more than 9,000 brilliant minds operating from 270 sites across 30 countries. Together we share an ambitious purpose to ‘Make tomorrow safer than today’.

 

 When failure in use is not an option, we help customers make certain that their products, materials, processes and services are safe, compliant and fit for purpose. From early R&D, through complex regulatory approvals and into production, our global laboratory network of scientists, engineers, and technologists support customers to achieve assurance over product quality, sustainable outcomes, and market access.

 

 While we are proud of our global reach, working at Element feels like being part of a smaller company. We empower you to take charge of your career, and reward excellence and integrity with growth and development.

 

 Industries across the world depend on our care, attention to detail and the absolute accuracy of our work. The role we have to play in creating a safer world is much bigger than our organization.

 Diversity Statement

 At Element, we always take pride in putting our people first. We are an equal opportunity employer that recognizes diversity and inclusion as fundamental to our Vision of becoming “the world’s most trusted testing partner”.

 

 All suitably qualified candidates will receive consideration for employment on the basis of objective work related criteria and without regard for the following: age, disability, ethnic origin, gender, marital status, race, religion, responsibility of dependents, sexual orientation, or gender identity or other characteristics in accordance with the applicable governing laws or other characteristics in accordance with the applicable governing laws.

V2I-A9A1418340FD.text:
Teradyne: Global Leaders in Test and Automation Teradyne is a global authority in test and automation, driving next-gen technology with advanced solutions. We ensure your electronic devices work flawlessly, and our industrial automation solutions streamline product development and delivery worldwide. 
 
 Our Production Support & Interfacing division offers a full range of service solutions, covering Teradyne test systems in 47+ countries. Our services span design, production, testing, and maintenance, delivered by 1,450+ professionals. 
 
 We attract, develop, and retain a high-performance workforce, comprised of people with diverse backgrounds and a shared drive for excellence. We strive to foster a positive and inclusive work environment that helps employees, and communities, thrive. Teradyne (NASDAQ: TER) is a global leader in advanced technology solutions. Our Semiconductor Test business delivers automated test equipment (ATE), including the UltraFLEX and UltraFLEXplus platforms, that helps the world’s leading semiconductor manufacturers ensure the quality and performance of the chips powering today’s electronics. Teradyne also includes a Robotics business (Universal Robots and Mobile Industrial Robots). 
 
 Opportunity Overview 
 The Teradyne Global Customer Support team is hiring a  Customer Support Production Manager to help build and lead the field production support organization that supports a local customer in the area. This leadership role manages Field Production Support Team Leads and, through them, the Production Support Engineers who support UltraFLEX and UltraFLEXplus ATE systems and test fixtures. 
 
 This role integrates organizational leadership, service operations, financial management, customer engagement, and cross-functional coordination. The manager translates customer production priorities into regional staffing, service-delivery, and improvement plans that support sustained operational performance. 
 
 For the first several quarters, you will be temporarily based at the Teradyne Austin, Texas office for onboarding and training before transitioning to the customer area in another TX-based location. You will help build the support team for the customer. The position partners closely with Global Customer Support leadership and reports to the US Operations Manager. 
 
 In this role, you will: 
 
 Organizational Leadership 
 Lead, coach, and develop a team of Field Production Support Team Leads, including onboarding, performance management, goal setting, and succession planning. 
 Oversee the capability, capacity, and engagement of the broader Production Support Engineer organization through your Team Leads, ensuring skills are aligned with customer and business requirements. 
 Foster a culture of accountability, knowledge sharing, standard processes, and continuous improvement across the region. 
 Make staffing, hiring, and resource-allocation decisions in partnership with HR and senior management. 
 
 Service Delivery & Operations 
 Own regional execution of Operational Support Services (OSS) commitments, including contracted and value-added activities, and ensure consistent, high-quality delivery across all assigned accounts. 
 Serve as the second-level escalation point for production-impacting issues, supporting Team Leads in resolution and engaging senior management and cross-functional partners when needed. 
 Monitor regional KPIs and system-performance data (e.g., uptime, response/resolution time, CSAT), identify gaps and trends, and drive corrective and continuous-improvement actions to closure. 
 Champion structured problem-solving and quality methodologies, including 8D, root cause analysis (RCA), 5 Whys, and Six Sigma, across the region. 
 
 Financial Management 
 Own the regional budget, including annual planning, quarterly forecasting, and monthly variance analysis for labor, travel, spare parts, and operating expenses. 
 Manage cost of service and productivity metrics, driving initiatives to improve efficiency without compromising quality or customer satisfaction. 
 Approve regional expenditures, overtime, and resource decisions within delegated authority; partner with Finance on reporting and compliance. 
 Contribute financial inputs and business cases for headcount growth, capital requests, and service-product investments. 
 
 Customer & Business Engagement 
 Build and maintain strong relationships with key customer stakeholders; participate in executive-level business reviews and satisfaction reviews alongside Team Leads. 
 Oversee customer expectations, escalations, and action items across the region, ensuring clear communication of status, risks, priorities, and improvement actions. 
 Support Marketing and Account Managers during service-contract renewal negotiations by providing relevant operational data and other information needed to support the negotiation process. 
 Collaborate with worldwide account teams, Sales, Marketing, Engineering, and Operations to align regional execution with global strategy. 
 
 What Success Looks Like 
 Regional OSS commitments are consistently met or exceeded, with customer satisfaction meeting or improving against established targets. 
 Team Leads and Production Support Engineers demonstrate sustained engagement, readiness for expanded responsibilities, and clear development and succession paths. 
 Regional budget delivered on plan, with predictable forecasting and improved cost of service. 
 Sustained improvement in uptime, escalation resolution, and recurring-failure reduction across the installed base. 
 
 NOTE:   This role will require the successful hire to train with our local team at our facility in Austin, TX for approximately one year from late calendar Y2026 through late calendar Y2027.  The successful hire will then relocate to another TX-based location and work from that area going forward. 
 
 What You’ll Gain 
 Structured onboarding and training at our Austin, Texas office 
 Executive-level exposure to leading semiconductor manufacturers through customer business reviews 
 Leadership development and opportunities to grow into broader management roles at Teradyne 
 Ownership of a regional budget and service-delivery results 
 Collaboration with worldwide account teams, Sales, Marketing, Engineering, and Operations 
 
 All About You 
 Required 
 A bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, electronics engineering, physics, business, or a related field, or equivalent experience directly applicable to semiconductor test, capital-equipment service, or production-support leadership. 
 At least eight years of relevant experience supporting ATE or semiconductor capital equipment in a high-volume manufacturing environment. 
 At least five years of people-management experience including leading Team Leads, supervisors, or managers in addition to individual contributors. 
 Demonstrated experience managing budgets and forecasts, with responsibility for regional or business-unit financial performance. 
 Experience with escalation management, service operations, and production improvement activities. 
 Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound judgment, customer focus, and the ability to work effectively with engineering, factory, sales, service, finance, and customer stakeholders. 
 Willingness and ability to work from the Teradyne Austin, Texas office for several quarters during onboarding and training. 
 Willingness and ability to travel approximately 30% of the time to support customer, team, and business needs. 
 Nice to Have 
 Hands-on familiarity with ATE platforms such as UltraFLEX or UltraFLEXplus. 
 Experience with financial planning tools and workforce/capacity planning in a service organization. 
 Prior experience in customer-facing service leadership roles or service-contract renewals. 
 Familiarity with structured problem-solving methodologies, including 8D, root cause analysis, 5 Whys, and Six Sigma, as well as ticketing and workflow tools. 
 
 
 This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. 
 Compensation 
 The base salary range for this role is $134,500-$215,200. This range is a good faith estimate, and the amount of base salary will correspond with experience and skill set. This range can also fluctuate depending on demand and location. 
 
 Incentive Plan: 
 This job is eligible for discretionary bonus(es) based on financial performance. 
 
 Benefits: 
 Teradyne offers a variety of robust health and well-being benefit programs, including medical, dental, vision, Flexible Spending Accounts, retirement savings plans, life and disability insurance, paid vacation & holidays, tuition assistance programs, and more. Please click here  to see details. 
 
 #LI-SN1

Position Summary
 The Director, Digital Twin & Intelligent Manufacturing Capabilities is responsible for defining and advancing the enterprise strategy, technology direction, governance, standards, and capability roadmap for Digital Twins, Process Twins, Process Intelligence, Modeling, Simulation, Automation-enabled Manufacturing, and AI-driven manufacturing capabilities across Global Technical Operations (GTO). This role serves as GTO's enterprise leader for Digital Twin and Process Intelligence capabilities and is accountable for shaping how manufacturing science, process knowledge, automation, data, advanced analytics, artificial intelligence, and digital technologies are leveraged to improve technology transfer, process understanding, manufacturing readiness, operational performance, and business outcomes across the product lifecycle.
 The Director will partner closely with MPAS, Tech Transfer, BPD, Singapore manufacturing and digital organizations, Alexion, FMC, Regional Digital Leads, Manufacturing, IT, Enterprise Architecture, Data & AI, Automation, and Site Digital teams to establish enterprise-scale capabilities and implementation frameworks that can be deployed consistently across the manufacturing network. While Regional Digital Leads and site organizations retain accountability for site-level deployment and adoption, this role is responsible for defining the enterprise capability strategy, technology direction, operating model, governance, standards, and reusable assets required to scale Digital Twin and Process Intelligence capabilities across GTO.
 This position requires deep expertise in Digital Twin and Intelligent Manufacturing capabilities, combined with strong technology leadership, manufacturing and process-science credibility, automation awareness, systems thinking, vendor evaluation experience, AI and advanced analytics fluency, and a proven ability to lead large-scale cross-functional transformation initiatives in complex global organizations.
   
 Key Responsibilities 
 Enterprise Strategy & Capability Leadership  
 Define and maintain the enterprise strategy for Digital Twins, Process Twins, Process Intelligence, Modeling, Simulation, and Intelligent Manufacturing capabilities across GTO. 
 Establish and evolve a multi-year capability roadmap aligned with GTO priorities, Digital Tech Transfer strategy, manufacturing modernization initiatives, and enterprise digital objectives. 
 Identify strategic opportunities to improve technology transfer, process characterization, scale-up, manufacturing readiness, process robustness, operational performance, and business value. 
 Develop capability maturity models, adoption frameworks, and value realization approaches to support enterprise scaling. 
 Translate business needs and manufacturing challenges into actionable capability roadmaps, standards, investment priorities, and implementation approaches. 
 Technology, Automation & Intelligent Manufacturing Leadership  
 Define how Digital Twins, manufacturing systems, automation environments, process data, simulation platforms, advanced analytics, machine learning, and AI capabilities work together as part of GTO’s Intelligent Manufacturing ecosystem. 
 Lead evaluation and selection of Digital Twin, Process Intelligence, Modeling, Simulation, and AI-enabled manufacturing technologies. 
 Drive technology strategy and investment recommendations across platforms, tools, vendors, and strategic partnerships. 
 Assess emerging technologies and industry developments to guide future capability investments and roadmap decisions. 
 Partner with Enterprise Architecture, IT, Data & AI, Automation, and Digital organizations to define scalable architectures, integration approaches, and operational models. 
 Establish approaches for connecting process knowledge, manufacturing systems, automation platforms, process data, simulations, and Digital Twins through effective data flows and information architectures. 
 Guide build-versus-buy decisions and strategic technology direction for Digital Twin and Intelligent Manufacturing capabilities. 
 Process Intelligence, Modeling & Digital Twin Governance  
 Establish governance frameworks, standards, methodologies, and best practices for Digital Twin and Process Intelligence capabilities across GTO. 
 Define and oversee model lifecycle management approaches, including model transition, deployment, maintenance, monitoring, documentation, and retirement. 
 Establish ownership models, stewardship expectations, support models, and decision-making frameworks for Digital Twin and Process Intelligence capabilities. 
 Develop reusable methods, templates, and standards that enable scalability and consistency across products, sites, and manufacturing networks. 
 Ensure Digital Twin and Process Intelligence initiatives are aligned to enterprise quality, regulatory, and operational expectations. 
 Community of Practice & Capability Development  
 Establish and lead the GTO Digital Twin & Process Intelligence Community of Practice and Center of Excellence. 
 Build and maintain a network of practitioners and subject matter experts across Manufacturing, MPAS, Tech Transfer, BPD, Automation, IT, Data & AI, Site Digital organizations, and Regional Digital Leads. 
 Develop standards, reference architectures, implementation guidance, training materials, and best practices to support capability maturity and enterprise adoption. 
 Promote innovation, knowledge sharing, and capability development across the organization. 
 Sponsor and oversee Digital Twin and Process Intelligence initiatives involving interns, graduate students, and university partnerships aligned to strategic business priorities. 
 Collaborate with academic institutions, innovation partners, and external research organizations to advance Digital Twin and Intelligent Manufacturing capabilities. 
 Enterprise Transformation & Business Partnership  
 Partner closely with MPAS, Tech Transfer, BPD, Singapore manufacturing organizations, Alexion, FMC, and Manufacturing organizations to identify opportunities and shape future-state capabilities. 
 Ensure Digital Twin and Process Intelligence strategies align with broader Digital Tech Transfer, Intelligent Manufacturing, and GTO transformation objectives. 
 Lead complex cross-functional initiatives requiring alignment across business, scientific, manufacturing, digital, and technology organizations. 
 Influence strategic decisions and drive organizational alignment without direct authority. 
 Translate emerging technologies into scalable business capabilities and measurable outcomes. 
 External Innovation & Vendor Management  
 Build and manage relationships with strategic technology vendors, industry organizations, academic partners, and innovation ecosystems. 
 Lead technology assessments, proof-of-concept initiatives, capability evaluations, and vendor-selection activities. 
 Monitor industry developments in Digital Twins, Process Intelligence, Manufacturing Analytics, Simulation, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Intelligent Manufacturing. 
 Guide strategic partnerships and investment decisions that strengthen GTO’s long-term Digital Twin and Process Intelligence capabilities. 
  
 Qualifications  
 Required 
 Advanced degree (Master’s or PhD) in Engineering, Manufacturing Systems, Chemical Engineering, Bioprocess Engineering, Data Science, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Operations Research, Life Sciences, or a related technical discipline. 
 12-20+ years of experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, manufacturing, engineering, automation, process development, digital transformation, or related industries. 
 Demonstrated experience leading enterprise-scale Digital Twin, Process Twin, Process Intelligence, Simulation, Advanced Analytics, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or Intelligent Manufacturing initiatives. 
 Strong understanding of manufacturing systems, automation environments, industrial data flows, manufacturing data ecosystems, and Intelligent Manufacturing concepts. 
 Experience evaluating technology platforms, software vendors, emerging technologies, and digital capabilities. 
 Demonstrated ability to develop capability roadmaps, guide technology investments, and establish enterprise governance and standards. 
 Strong understanding of AI, machine learning, advanced analytics, simulation technologies, and their practical application in manufacturing and process environments. 
 Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional transformation initiatives in highly matrixed organizations. 
 Proven ability to influence senior scientific, manufacturing, business, and technology stakeholders without direct authority. 
 Excellent executive communication, stakeholder engagement, facilitation, and leadership skills.  
 Preferred  
 Experience in biologics manufacturing, process development, manufacturing sciences, technology transfer, or technical operations. 
 Experience working across BPD, MPAS, Manufacturing, Tech Transfer, Automation, IT, Data & AI, and Enterprise Architecture organizations. 
 Familiarity with Digital Twin and Process Intelligence platforms such as BaseTwo, M-Star, FlexSim, BioSolve, Solvace, AspenTech, AVEVA, or similar ecosystems. 
 Experience establishing enterprise communities of practice, governance models, capability-development programs, or Centers of Excellence. 
 Experience leading innovation partnerships, university collaborations, internship programs, or applied research initiatives.

This is where  your work makes a difference.
 
 At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.
 
 Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.
 
 Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride. 
 
 
 
 Your Role 
 The Sr. Manager - Quality - Visual Inspection & Particulate Control provides strategic and technical Quality leadership for manufacturing and laboratory quality systems, with a focus on Visual Inspection and particulate matter control for injectable products. This role ensures that inspection programs, qualification/validation, particulate investigations, and associated controls are scientifically sound, risk-based, well documented, and aligned with regulatory requirements, compendial expectations, and the company Quality Management System.
 
 What You'll Be Doing 
 Lead Quality oversight for manual, semi-automated, and automated visual inspection programs, ensuring inspection processes remain effective, compliant, and aligned with patient safety expectations.
 Develop and maintain risk-based particulate control strategies that strengthen defect prevention, improve manufacturing controls, and reduce product quality risks.
 Provide technical leadership for qualification and validation activities related to visual inspection systems, ensuring studies are scientifically sound, appropriately designed, and fully documented.
 Direct complex investigations involving visible particulate matter, inspection trends, and product quality events, driving objective root cause analysis and effective corrective actions.
 Partner with Operations, Engineering, Laboratory, and Quality teams to identify opportunities for process improvement, defect reduction, and continuous enhancement of inspection performance.
 Support regulatory inspections, customer audits, and health authority interactions by providing expertise, documentation, and responses related to visual inspection and particulate control programs.
 Establish and monitor quality performance metrics, trend analyses, and risk indicators to proactively identify emerging issues and ensure sustainable improvements.
 
 What You'll Bring 

 Required Qualifications
 Bachelor's degree in Pharmacy, Chemistry, Biology, Microbiology, Engineering, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related scientific or technical discipline.
 Typically 10+ years of progressive experience within pharmaceutical, biopharmaceutical, medical device, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments, including significant Quality leadership responsibilities.
 Demonstrated expertise in visual inspection programs for injectable or sterile products, including inspection strategy, defect classification, qualification programs, and performance monitoring.
 Experience leading complex investigations, risk assessments, corrective and preventive action (CAPA) programs, validation activities, and regulatory inspection responses.
 Strong knowledge of current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) and applicable compendial requirements, including USP and USP .
 Experience making science-based quality decisions involving product disposition, compliance risk management, and quality system effectiveness.
 Strong communication, collaboration, and influencing skills with the ability to build alignment across multiple functions while maintaining independent quality judgment.
 Leadership experience through direct people leadership, matrix leadership, or technical leadership roles.
 
 Preferred Qualifications
 Advanced degree in Pharmaceutical Sciences, Chemistry, Microbiology, Engineering, or a related discipline.
 Experience supporting commercial sterile manufacturing operations for injectable pharmaceutical products.
 Expertise in particulate characterization techniques, defect identification, and contamination control strategies.
 Experience implementing continuous improvement initiatives that improve inspection effectiveness, defect prevention, and process capability.
 Experience interacting directly with the FDA, Health Canada, EMA, or other global regulatory agencies.
 Certification or advanced training in Quality Risk Management, Lean Six Sigma, or related continuous improvement methodologies.
 
 We understand compensation is an important factor as you consider the next step in your career. At Baxter, we are committed to equitable pay for all employees, and we strive to be more transparent with our pay practices. The estimated base salary for this position is $136,000 - $187,000 annually. The estimated salary is meant to reflect an anticipated salary range for the position. We may pay more or less than the anticipated range based upon market data and other factors, all of which are subject to change. Individual pay is based on location, skills and expertise, experience, and other relevant factors. This position may also be eligible for discretionary bonuses. For questions about this, our pay philosophy, and available benefits, please speak to the recruiter if you decide to apply and are selected for an interview.

 Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.
 
 
 US Benefits at Baxter (except for Puerto Rico)

Our health and well-being benefits include medical and dental coverage that start on day one, as well as insurance coverage for basic life, accident, short-term and long-term disability, and business travel accident insurance. Financial and retirement benefits include the Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP), with the ability to purchase company stock at a discount, and the 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan (RSP), with options for employee contributions and company matching. We also offer Flexible Spending Accounts, educational assistance programs, and time-off benefits such as paid holidays, paid time off ranging from 20 to 35 days based on length of service, family and medical leaves of absence, and paid parental leave. Additional benefits include commuting benefits, the Employee Discount Program, the Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and childcare benefits. Join us and enjoy the competitive compensation and benefits we offer to our employees. For additional information regarding Baxter US Benefits, please speak with your recruiter or visit our Benefits site: Benefits | Baxter 
 
 
 Equal Employment Opportunity 
 
 Baxter is an equal opportunity employer. Baxter evaluates qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, protected veteran status, disability/handicap status or any other legally protected characteristic.
